facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH THE PERMIT, NOT THE PRODUCT. North Myrtle Beach is the one town in the batch that passed a brand-new, specific, still-warm rule that decides whether a turf installation counts against a homeowner's lot coverage — § 23-129.4, adopted 6-0 on 6 October 2025. Under it a surface is impervious by default; the burden is on the applicant to prove 2 inches per hour of infiltration with manufacturer certification sheets, an inspected base built to spec, and an ongoing maintenance duty. That turns the installer's paperwork into the product. The page should open on the sentence 'in North Myrtle Beach your turf is impervious until you prove otherwise — here is the submittal package we hand your permit office,' then say plainly that pool decks count and pool basins don't. The second half of the page belongs to the 62.6% vacancy rate and the 62.5 median age: this is a town of owners who are not here nine months a year, so the pitch is about a yard that looks the same to a rental guest in February as it did in July with nobody watering it, and about salt and marsh conditions in Cherry Grove that kill sod. That is a completely different page from Myrtle Beach next door — which is a municipal-fields sales pitch to a parks department — and from Conway, which is a flood-and-slow-soil engineering pitch to year-round working families. For NMB commercial, the ERU math is the hook: 3,500 sq ft of impervious area is one ERU at $10 a month, so proving perviousness is a line item, not a nicety.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa:
THE STRONGEST VERIFIED ORDINANCE FINDING IN THIS ENTIRE BATCH. North Myrtle Beach zoning text amendment ZTX-25-8 amended Chapter 23 § 23-2 (Definitions) and added new § 23-129.4. Planning Commission public hearing 22 July 2025, recommended unanimously, no public comment; first reading 18 August 2025; SECOND READING PASSED 6-0 at the City Council meeting of 6 October 2025. What it does: it redefines 'impervious surface' as anything that prevents or significantly impedes infiltration, and adds the sentence that matters — 'Surfaces shall be considered impervious UNLESS demonstrated otherwise in accordance with the performance criteria set forth in Section 23-129.4.' To be counted pervious, a system must demonstrate a minimum infiltration rate of TWO INCHES PER HOUR based on manufacturer testing or accepted industry standards, be installed per manufacturer specifications including required base materials, be inspected to confirm installation matches the approved specs, and be maintained by the owner to preserve infiltration over time. If those criteria are not met 'the surface will be considered impervious, regardless of material type or labeling.' Applicants must submit manufacturer specification sheets and construction details with the permit. It applies only to single-family and duplex residential not subject to site-specific development plan review; commercial, multifamily and institutional go through the more rigorous site-plan stormwater process. Swimming pool basins are exempted from impervious calculation; pool decks and surrounding hardscape are not. At second reading the Planning & Development director stated this only bites when the 40 percent pervious ratio is exceeded, and that the manufacturer's certification sheet must accompany the permit application. Note: the ordinance does NOT name artificial turf — I searched the city site and it does not appear — but it is the operative rule for it, because a turf system over compacted aggregate is exactly the 'decorative surface that does not meaningfully reduce runoff' the staff report was written to catch.
ALSO VERIFIED: NMB stormwater utility fees effective 1 July 2026 — single-family residential $10.00/month, condo $7.50/month, COMMERCIAL $10.00 per ERU per month, where one ERU = 3,500 square feet of impervious area. So on a commercial site, every 3,500 sq ft that gets classed impervious is another $120 a year, forever. NMB also requires a Tree Removal Permit.
Statewide: SC Code § 27-30-130 — HOA rules must be recorded with the Horry County Register of Deeds and re-recorded annually by January 10 to stay enforceable.
facts.turf_specifics: The most drainage-constrained and most salt-exposed town in the batch. Oceanfront and dune-ridge lots are Newhan-type dune sand: excessively drained, very rapid permeability, no regular water table, shell fragments to 35% by volume — great infiltration, but shelly sand complicates base compaction and wind-driven sand continuously loads the pile. Behind the dune line and through Cherry Grove the ground drops into coastal flatwoods and tidal-marsh-adjacent soils with seasonal high water tables. Cherry Grove is threaded with man-made saltwater canals and backs onto salt marsh, so lots there have brackish groundwater within inches at high tide, salt spray, and tidal-flooding exposure. Elevation 26 ft city-wide but far lower on the Cherry Grove spit. Salt exposure is the highest of the four towns: specify UV and salt-tolerant backing, non-corroding fasteners, and expect the client to hose down for salt as well as for pets.
facts.housing_stock: 2020 census: 18,790 residents but 25,950 housing units, of which 62.6% were VACANT. That single number defines the town — there are 1.4 housing units per resident. Median age 62.5, the oldest in the batch by more than 20 years over Conway. Average home built 1996. About 52% of residents own their home free and clear; ~22% rent. City formed in 1968 from the merger of four separate beach towns — Cherry Grove Beach, Crescent Beach, Ocean Drive Beach and Windy Hill Beach — and each still reads as its own neighbourhood with its own stock: Cherry Grove is a low-lying spit of canal-front and marsh-front cottages and raised houses running to the North Carolina line; Ocean Drive is the historic Main Street core; Crescent Beach and Windy Hill are heavier on oceanfront condo towers. Inland of Highway 17 sits a completely different product — Barefoot Resort and the golf-course HOA communities, newer, larger-lot, covenant-governed. Total area 22.31 sq mi, elevation 26 ft.
facts.who_lives_there: Retirees and second-home owners, overwhelmingly. Median age 62.5. The 62.6% vacancy figure is not distress, it is seasonality: most of these units are owned by someone who is not in South Carolina from September to May, or are in a rental management program. The year-round population is small, older, and heavily owner-occupied-outright. Practical consequence for this business: the decision-maker is frequently not on site, is buying to eliminate a maintenance obligation they can't supervise from Ohio or Ontario, and cares about what the property looks like to a rental guest. Tourist volume is enormous and the Main Street Ocean Drive shag-dancing scene draws a specific, loyal repeat crowd.
facts.golf: Barefoot Resort, 4980 Barefoot Resort Bridge Rd, North Myrtle Beach 29582 — four championship courses by Greg Norman, Davis Love III, Tom Fazio and Pete Dye, opened April 2000, named 2016 North American Golf Resort of the Year by IAGTO; reached by a swing bridge relocated from North Carolina. Tidewater Golf Club — set between the Intracoastal Waterway and Cherry Grove Inlet with nine holes playing along the tidal inlet, ranked among the nation's top 100 public courses. Also in or immediately adjacent (locally well known, verify addresses before publishing): Surf Golf & Beach Club, Beachwood Golf Club, Possum Trot Golf Club, Robbers Roost, Eagle Nest and Long Bay Golf Club just west toward Little River. Barefoot in particular is the right reference for a residential putting-green pitch — the customers who bought there bought for golf.
facts.commercial_targets:
NORTH MYRTLE BEACH PARK & SPORTS COMPLEX, 150 Citizens Circle, Little River SC 29566 — the biggest single municipal prospect in the batch and it is ALL NATURAL GRASS. Current inventory after expansion: 12 baseball/softball fields, 13 soccer/lacrosse fields, 16 batting cages, 5 playgrounds, 11 picnic shelters, 3 miles of walking trails, a 10-acre meadow, an amphitheatre, a nature preserve, an administrative building, and the Waggin Tails Dog Parks (separate small-dog and large-dog enclosures). The Phase II expansion broke ground May 2024 and was COMPLETED NOVEMBER 2025, adding 5 soccer fields, 6 baseball fields, freshwater ponds, walking trails, 2 playgrounds and picnic shelters; the first tournament on the expanded fields was February 2026 and drew 70 teams from 14 states. The city's own project page says youth participation in baseball, softball and soccer keeps growing and the expansion exists to host multiple simultaneous tournaments. A city that just finished a two-and-a-half-year, multi-field grass expansion is a maintenance-burden conversation, not a cold call. Parks contact 843-281-3800.
The dog park rules page is a gift for a pet-turf pitch — it literally instructs owners 'Do not let dogs dig holes; if they do please fill them in immediately.'
OTHER: J. North Myrtle Beach Aquatic & Fitness Center. McLean Park. Barefoot Resort and Tidewater for practice greens and clubhouse surrounds. Schools: North Myrtle Beach High (Chiefs), NMB Middle, Ocean Drive Elementary, Waterway Elementary, Riverside Elementary (Horry County Schools). NOTE: I could not verify specific named doggy-daycare or childcare businesses inside NMB city limits — the directory sites blocked retrieval. Treat that as a to-do, not a gap to paper over.

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH THE SCHOOL AND SPORTS-FIELD PITCH, because Burgess is the one place in this batch where the owner's stated target actually exists at scale. St. James High School on Highway 707 has a 5,000-seat stadium, three practice fields, a softball diamond and a baseball field, and it anchors a five-school feeder complex serving a community that went from 3,000 people to 32,000 in thirty years — on land that is roughly 30% wetlands and water, where residents publicly testify that it floods in heavy storms. That is the whole page in one sentence: fields that cannot drain, in a community that will not stop growing, on ground that stays wet. Frame synthetic conversion as playable days per season and rain-out recovery, not as appearance — that is the language a school AD and a county rec director actually budget in. THE SECOND LEAD, distinct from every other town here, is the golf-community homeowner and the HOA amenity: TPC/Prince Creek, Blackmoor, International Club, Indigo Creek, Island Green, Myrtle Beach Golf & Yacht Club — people who bought a lot on a Fazio or a Gary Player course and want a private green that matches it, plus roughly 60 POAs with common areas and pool surrounds. THIRD, turn the paperwork into the differentiator: Burgess is unincorporated with ~60 separate POAs and county stormwater review, so say plainly that you handle covenant submittals and county land-disturbance permitting — in Burgess the paperwork IS the objection. VOICE: do not write this like Murrells Inlet's fishing-village page or like Carolina Forest's master-planned page. Burgess's actual identity is a rural African American farming settlement named for a postmaster that got swallowed by golf subdivisions in a single generation and is right now fighting a 2,000-4,000-home rezoning beside its own high school. That tension — old rural land versus new density, wet ground versus more rooftops — is the page's real register, and drainage is the word that connects the sales pitch to the thing residents are already arguing about at county council.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: Burgess is UNINCORPORATED, so there is no town code — Horry County zoning and stormwater rules apply, and the binding day-to-day constraint is HOA/POA covenants across roughly 60 separate subdivisions. Named bodies to know: Blackmoor Property Owners Association; the Greater Burgess Community Association (a civic association covering ~60 neighborhoods — influential but NOT itself an HOA); the Burgess Community Area Plan, adopted by Horry County Council in 2012 as the long-range guiding document. No artificial-turf-specific rule was found at county or HOA level, but per-subdivision covenants are the real gate and will vary. Also live: SCDOT has an active SC 707 (Socastee Blvd) Corridor Safety Improvement Project, and Horry County has demanded a Southern Evacuation Lifeline (SELL) agreement from developers. GAP: county ordinance text unreadable (site down, Municode 403) — verify per-subdivision covenants and county thresholds directly.
facts.turf_specifics: WATER IS THE DEFINING FACT AND IT IS THE PAGE'S BEST TECHNICAL HOOK. Roughly 30% of the Burgess area's acreage is wetlands or open water (GBCA). The Waccamaw River forms the western boundary; terrain is flat (county high point is 124 ft). The most-contested development tract in the area — the Bumgardner/Wall family tract between St. James High School and Blackmoor golf course — is described as roughly half wetlands, and residents state plainly that the area floods during heavy storms and that 'stormwater and different environmental issues' are the central problem. That means: seasonally high water table, low-lying poorly drained coastal-plain soils across much of the community, and lots where natural lawn stays soggy and where a badly built synthetic base will simply hold water. No meaningful salt exposure inland; only the eastern edge near US 17 Bypass sees any. Golf-community lots are graded to drain into HOA stormwater ponds, so any install must respect the existing grade and the HOA's stormwater easements. GAP: I could not read the Burgess Community Area Plan PDF or Horry County's stormwater ordinance — horrycountysc.gov refused connections on every attempt (ECONNREFUSED, 64.138.212.22) — and NRCS soil data timed out. Verify county land-disturbance thresholds and any impervious-surface limit before publishing a permitting claim.
facts.housing_stock: NOT a thin small place — this is the largest opportunity in the batch by a wide margin. Roughly 28 sq mi and about 32,000 people, bounded by the Waccamaw River on the west, US 17 Bypass on the east, the Horry-Georgetown county line on the south, and SC 31 / SC 707 on the north. Greater Burgess Community Association data: 17,044 parcels across 17,939 acres, 12,318 structures, and a neighborhood network covering roughly 60 named communities and over 8,000 homes. DOMINANT ERA IS 1990-PRESENT master-planned subdivisions — population went from ~3,000 in 1990 to ~25,000 in 2010 to ~31,000-32,000 by 2018-2020. Stock is therefore mostly 1990s-2020s production and semi-custom single-family homes on modest platted lots inside HOA subdivisions, plus golf-course lots, plus a still-substantial rural remainder (77.3% of parcels remain rural-density). HOA PREVALENCE IS THE HIGHEST IN THIS BATCH — the exact inverse of Loris. Named subdivisions include Blackmoor, Prince Creek and its many villages (Bellwood Landing, Collins Creek Landing, Creek Harbor, Creekhaven, Highwood, Hunters Grove, Laurel Bay, Linksbrook, Marcliff West, Seasons, Stonegate, Waverly Bay, Willow Bay, The Bays), International Club and its villages (Cambridge, Enclave, Grand Vistas, The Glens, The Villas), Indigo Creek, Island Green, Myrtle Beach Golf & Yacht Club, Cypress River Plantation, Creek Ridge Plantation, Wilderness Plantation, Kings Grant, Fox Hollow Plantation, Pines of St. James, The Meadows of St. Patrick, Laurel Woods, Summer Lakes, Woodland Park, Wynbrooke. Mixed year-round and retiree, with strong second-home and relocation inflow. NOTE: Burgess is unincorporated with no census place, so there is no official Burgess median income or home value; adjoining Murrells Inlet CDP (sharing the 29576 ZIP) runs $77,438 median household income, $366,000 median property value, 86% homeownership — usable as a stated proxy, not as a Burgess figure.
facts.who_lives_there: Three distinct populations layered on one another. (1) Retirees and Northeast/Midwest relocation buyers in the golf communities — Prince Creek/TPC, Blackmoor, International Club, Myrtle Beach Golf & Yacht Club, Indigo Creek, Island Green. (2) Year-round working families feeding the St. James school complex — St. James High alone enrols 1,880. (3) Long-tenured rural landowners who predate the 1990 build-out; the area was an African American farming community in the late 1800s, established as Marlow (post office, May 6, 1880) and renamed Burgess on August 15, 1906 for postmaster William Burgess, who served from 1887 until his death in 1934. The civic culture is organised and vocal: the Greater Burgess Community Association has fought density since the Burgess Community Area Plan was adopted by Horry County Council in 2012, and over 200 residents turned out for one rezoning hearing.
facts.golf: The densest golf concentration in this batch, all on or immediately off the SC 707 spine. TPC of Myrtle Beach — Tom Fazio design, opened 1999, off SC Highway 707 inside the Prince Creek development, par 72 at 6,950 yards, host of the 2000 Senior Tour Championship. Blackmoor Golf Club — Gary Player design, Longwood Road, Murrells Inlet, adjoining the Blackmoor subdivision and its POA, 6,614 yards. International Club of Myrtle Beach — 1560 International Club Blvd, Murrells Inlet SC 29576. Indigo Creek Golf Club — Willard Byrd design. Island Green Golf Club. Myrtle Beach Golf & Yacht Club. Within a short drive south: Prestwick, Wachesaw, Caledonia Golf & Fish Club, Pawleys Plantation, Willbrook Plantation.
facts.commercial_targets: THIS IS THE BATCH'S BEST LIST AND IT MAPS DIRECTLY ONTO WHAT THE OWNER SAID HE WANTS. St. James High School, 10800 Highway 707 — 1,880 students, a 5,000-seat football/soccer stadium ringed by an eight-lane track, THREE PRACTICE FIELDS, A SOFTBALL DIAMOND, A BASEBALL FIELD and four tennis courts; state titles in AAA girls softball (2006-07), AAA boys 4x400 relay (2008-09) and AAA boys baseball (2010-11). Its five feeder schools, all in or serving Burgess: St. James Middle, St. James Intermediate, St. James Elementary, Burgess Elementary, Seaside Elementary — each with fields. Golf facilities for practice greens, tee lines and clubhouse landscape: TPC of Myrtle Beach, Blackmoor Golf Club, International Club of Myrtle Beach, Indigo Creek Golf Club, Island Green, Myrtle Beach Golf & Yacht Club. Roughly 60 HOAs/POAs with common areas, amenity centers and pool surrounds — Blackmoor POA, the Prince Creek villages, the International Club villages. The community center near Mt. Zion Church. GAP: named daycares and pet daycare/boarding businesses along the 707 corridor could not be verified (search budget exhausted, county site down) — run a Google Business pass on 29588 and 29576 along SC 707 before writing that section; given ~8,000 homes and five schools, they certainly exist.
facts.landmarks: SC Highway 707 — the spine of the community, chronically congested, with an active SCDOT safety improvement project. St. James High School at 10800 Highway 707, about six miles from the ocean. The Waccamaw River (west boundary) and US 17 Bypass (east boundary). SC Highway 31, Carolina Bays Parkway, at the north. Blackmoor golf course and the Blackmoor community. TPC of Myrtle Beach and Prince Creek. Mt. Zion Church and the community center beside it. The Murrells Inlet MarshWalk just to the south. The Bumgardner tract — the contested land between St. James High and Blackmoor now proposed for 2,000-4,000 homes. The Marlow-to-Burgess post office renaming (1906) and the community's origin as a late-1800s African American farming settlement.

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH: 'The only town out here where people actually live year-round — and the one place a turf install doesn't need a town stormwater permit.' Shallotte is the outlier in this batch on every demographic axis: 6.8% vacancy against 15.8% / 35.8% / 55.1% next door, and a median age of 49.7 against 56.4 / 66.0 / 68.0. Its neighbours are retirement and vacation towns; Shallotte is the working town that serves them. That drives a completely different offer. The beach-town pages sell a low-maintenance yard to a 68-year-old who is away five months a year. The Shallotte page sells (a) COMMERCIAL AND INSTITUTIONAL work — three schools, the town's four parks, Planet Fun, the two shopping centres, and the daycare play areas that the UDO requires be fenced to four feet; and (b) FAMILY AND PET turf — the households with children and dogs that simply do not exist in the same numbers in Sunset Beach or Carolina Shores. The differentiating technical proof point is the permit threshold: Shallotte's stormwater permit triggers at ONE ACRE of disturbance, while Sunset Beach's triggers at a 200-square-foot increase in impervious surface. Same county, fifteen minutes apart, a ~218x difference. Say that plainly — it is checkable, it is genuinely useful, and no competitor's template page will have it. Second proof point: the UDO requires an irrigation system wherever non-drought-tolerant vegetation is planted, and requires trees and shrubs to survive on natural rainfall once established. Turf is the way out of that requirement. Do NOT lead with golf here — River's Edge is the only confirmed course in town, and Shallotte's real identity is the crossroads, not the fairway. Save putting greens for Calabash and Sunset Beach.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: Shallotte's UDO (town copy dated 2026-03-24) gives the most turf-favorable regulatory picture in this batch, and that is a page-worthy fact in itself. (1) STORMWATER TRIGGER IS ONE ACRE. A Town of Shallotte Storm Water Permit is required for new non-residential or residential development that will 'ultimately result in disturbance of one acre or more of land,' or for new development within 30 feet of intermittent and perennial streams or other water bodies. A normal residential turf install does not come close to an acre — so unlike Sunset Beach (200 sq ft), a backyard job here triggers no town stormwater plan. (2) 30-FOOT RIPARIAN BUFFER maintained on all sides of intermittent and perennial streams and other water bodies — this does bite on the many lots backing onto the Shallotte River and its creeks. (3) BUILT-UPON AREA is defined broadly as 'that portion of a development project that is covered by impervious or partially impervious cover including buildings, pavement, gravel roads, and recreation facilities' — note 'recreation facilities' is named, which is the phrase that could be read onto a sport court or large turf area on a commercial site. Critically, Shallotte's UDO contains NO list of pervious exclusions and NO alternative-materials certification path (Sunset Beach has both), and the phrase 'artificial turf' / 'synthetic turf' does not appear anywhere in the document. So on a commercial site the classification is an open question to be settled with staff, not a settled entitlement. (4) 'Lot Coverage' is defined narrowly as the portion of a lot occupied by a structure — not paving — with a 50% maximum in at least one district. (5) DAY CARE, and this is the direct commercial hook: 'All children's outside play areas shall be enclosed with at least a four-foot high fence,' plus minimum paved off-street parking and a paved loading/unloading area for at least two cars. (6) KENNELS: a screen of dense plant material at least three feet high where a proposed kennel abuts a residential lot. (7) LANDSCAPING/IRRIGATION — the strongest sales hook in the code: required trees and shrubs 'shall be drought tolerant and able to survive on natural rainfall once established,' a water source must be supplied within 100 feet of any planting requiring continuing watering, and 'where non-native or non-drought tolerant native vegetation is incorporated, an irrigation system shall be required.' Artificial turf sidesteps that mandate entirely. Also: mulch is required as ground cover on plantings, and disturbed ground must be vegetated with permanent grass or sod within 30 days of construction.
facts.turf_specifics: Mainland Atlantic Coastal Plain flatwoods, not dune sand — this is the key technical split from Sunset Beach's island. The regionally dominant soil pattern is the Leon series: very poorly to poorly drained, with a dark organic spodic Bh horizon (a hardpan) occurring within 30 inches of the surface, and a seasonal high water table that sits between 6 and 18 inches for several months a year and 18–36 inches for 2–10 months a year. Permeability is moderate to moderately slow through that Bh layer. Practical consequence: you cannot assume the subgrade will percolate. Turf base here needs designed positive drainage — fall to a daylighted outlet or a drain field — because the hardpan perches water under the base and the seasonal water table can come up into it. The Shallotte River is tidal through town, so riverfront and creek-backing lots add brackish influence and a 30-ft regulated riparian buffer. Salt exposure is materially lower than the beach towns — Shallotte is roughly 8–10 miles inland of the ocean and 26 ft in elevation. CAVEAT: Leon is documented as regionally extensive in the NC coastal plain (USDA Official Series Description); I did not verify parcel-level soil mapping for Shallotte specifically.
facts.housing_stock: 1,946 housing units with only 6.8% vacancy — by far the lowest of the four and the tell that this is a year-round town, not a resort. 1,814 households: 49.8% married-couple, 32% female householder with no partner, 27.9% living alone. Median age 49.7 — roughly 17 years younger than Carolina Shores and 18 younger than Sunset Beach. 18.4% under 18, 28.7% 65+. Population 4,185 (2020), up 13.9% from 3,675 in 2010. Incorporated 1899, the oldest incorporation in this batch, so the stock is genuinely mixed rather than single-era: an older platted core near the Shallotte River plus post-2000 subdivision and highway-corridor growth spreading along US 17 across 9.31 sq mi. Town elevation 26 ft. Not a master-planned HOA town in the way Carolina Shores is — HOA coverage is patchy and concentrated in the newer subdivisions and in River's Edge, rather than blanket. NOTE: parcel-level lot-size data and an HOA-coverage count were not verified this session.
facts.who_lives_there: Working, year-round families — the only town in this batch where that is true. The 6.8% vacancy rate, the 49.7 median age, and the 18.4% share under 18 all point the same way. Shallotte is the retail, medical, school and services hub for the whole west end of Brunswick County: the beach towns (Sunset Beach, Ocean Isle, Holden) have the retirees and the rental houses, and Shallotte has the people who work in them, plus the schools their children attend. It is also the shopping trip for those beach-town retirees, which is why the commercial corridor is oversized for a town of 4,185.

name: Grissettown

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH THE BACKYARD PUTTING GREEN, BUILT ON A BASE — NOT ON BRUNSWICK LOAM. Grissettown is the highest ground in this batch (43.7 ft) sitting in the most expensive ZIP ($463,200 median value in 28469), 2.7 miles from Ocean Ridge Plantation's 72 holes and 3.4 from Sea Trail's three courses, in housing whose median build year is 2001. That is a precise customer: a golf-community homeowner who plays four courses within five miles and wants a green at home. The technical hook that makes the page credible and is TRUE ONLY HERE: the centroid soil is Goldsboro fine sandy loam over an Aquic Paleudult subsoil, and within one neighbourhood the seasonal high water table swings from 48 inches on a Baymeade sand ridge to 6 inches on a Lynchburg flat. So the page argues that a green here is a drainage build, not a carpet — you cut to a base, you engineer fall, you find an outlet, and you never assume the native loam percs. WHY THIS DIFFERS FROM ITS NEIGHBOURS: Seaside, 3.4 miles down the same NC 904, is 30 feet lower and sits on dune sand and tidal marsh — the opposite failure mode; its page leads with salt and water-table extremes. Thomasboro leads with full-time retirees and wet flatwoods, not golf. Civietown has no golf within six miles at all and leads with schools and fields. Grissettown is the only one of the four that is simultaneously high, dry-ish, wealthy, and ringed by championship golf — so it is the putting-green page, and it should be the one that carries the county's Impervious Surface definition question ('compacted earth and gravel are named impervious; artificial turf is not named — here is how we handle that with the county') because that is the credibility beat a golf-community buyer actually needs.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: Unincorporated — governed by the Brunswick County Unified Development Ordinance (revision dated 1/28/2025, adopted under NCGS Chapter 160D), administered from 75 Courthouse Dr, Bldg I, Bolivia NC. THE MATERIAL FINDING: the UDO's definition of Impervious Surface reads 'Any surface which in whole or in part, restricts or prevents the natural absorption of water into the ground. Such surfaces may include, but not be limited to compacted earth (such as marl and coquina), gravel, concrete, asphalt, or other paving material, and all area covered by the footprint of buildings or structures. Porous pavement, uncovered wooden slatted decks and the water area of a swimming pool are considered pervious.' Artificial turf is NOT named either way — but 'compacted earth' and 'gravel' ARE named as impervious, and a conventional turf install is compacted aggregate over compacted subgrade. That is a real, checkable, unresolved question the page can own: confirm base build with the county Stormwater Administrator before design. UDO 3.9.1 confirms a Brunswick County Stormwater Permit may be required and directs applicants to the separate Stormwater Ordinance. Fence heights, UDO 6.10.1: RR and R-7500 allow 6 ft in the front yard and 6 ft in all other yards, 8 ft with administrative adjustment; R-6000, SBR-6000 and MR-3200 allow only 4 ft in the front yard, 6 ft elsewhere, 8 ft with adjustment — directly relevant to dog runs and pet turf enclosures. Viewshed Protection Overlay applies within 300 ft of normal high water on the Shallotte River (designated for all unincorporated areas of Brunswick County) and the Intracoastal Waterway. HOA GAP: covenant text for Ocean Ridge Plantation, Sea Trail and Thistle on artificial turf could not be obtained from public sources — the client should pull the actual CC&Rs and ARB guidelines before publishing any claim about HOA approval.
facts.turf_specifics: USGS elevation at the hamlet centroid: 43.7 ft — the HIGHEST of the four in this batch. USDA SSURGO at the centroid: Goldsboro fine sandy loam, 0 to 2 percent slopes (87% Goldsboro, moderately well drained; 7% Norfolk, well drained; 6% Lynchburg, somewhat poorly drained). Within a ~1.2 km box the full palette is Baymeade fine sand (well drained) and Norfolk loamy fine sand (well drained) on the ridges; Goldsboro, Foreston and Tomahawk (moderately well drained) on the flats; and Leon fine sand, Lumbee, Grifton, Muckalee, Rains, Murville, Pantego and Torhunta (poorly to very poorly drained) in the pockets. The practical point: Goldsboro is an Aquic Paleudult — a loamy surface over a dense, slowly permeable subsoil. SSURGO seasonal-high-water-table depths for Brunswick County (NC019): Leon, Rains, Lynchburg and Muckalee all reach within about 6 inches of the surface; Foreston and Tomahawk about 24 inches; Baymeade and Norfolk about 48 inches. So on one street you can hit a 48-inch water table on a Baymeade ridge and a 6-inch one on a Lynchburg flat. That is the whole drainage argument for this town: percolation cannot be assumed, the base has to be engineered and the outlet has to be found, and native-soil putting greens fail here because the loam holds water on the subsoil. Salt exposure is low — 5.6 mi from the Ocean Isle strand, no direct aerosol load, unlike Seaside.
facts.housing_stock: RESEARCH FLAG: no census place, no population figure, no municipal government exists for Grissettown itself — it is an OSM/GNIS 'hamlet' with no boundary. Best available proxy is ZCTA 28469 (Ocean Isle Beach), which is a much larger area than the hamlet and skews toward the barrier island. ACS 2023 5-yr for 28469: 9,258 housing units, median year built 2001, median home value $463,200 (highest of the four ZIPs in this batch), 87.3% of occupied units owner-occupied. Occupancy is the tell: only 4,719 units (51%) are occupied; 3,557 units (38.4% of ALL housing stock) are classed 'for seasonal, recreational, or occasional use.' On the ground Grissettown itself is the inland, non-island half of that ZIP — scattered older frontage along NC 904 and Old Shallotte Road NW, plus 1990s–2000s golf-community subdivisions filling in toward Ocean Ridge Plantation. Governing lot standards are Brunswick County UDO Table 4-1 (unincorporated land, not a town code): RR requires 20,000 sf minimum lot without water/sewer or 15,000 sf with; R-7500 requires 15,000 sf without or 7,500 sf with; R-6000/SBR-6000 10,000 sf without or 6,000 sf with. Front yard 25 ft, side 5–10 ft. HOA prevalence: high inside the named plantations, effectively zero on the old road frontage — two different customers on the same page.
facts.who_lives_there: Median age in ZCTA 28469 is 61.2 (M 60.9 / F 61.3). The 38% seasonal-use share means the ZIP as a whole is a second-home market, but Grissettown proper sits ~5.6 mi inland from the Ocean Isle Beach strand and ~4.6 mi from Sunset Beach, so the hamlet itself is the year-round side of a heavily seasonal ZIP: retirees and near-retirees in golf-community houses, plus longtime local families on the original Grissettown road frontage. 87% owner occupancy means almost nobody here is a renter you can't sell to.

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH THE TOWN CODE AND THE SALT. Surfside Beach is the only incorporated municipality on this list, and the only place where a written number decides whether the job happens: maximum impervious coverage 40% in R-1, 45% in R-2, 50% in R-3, plus a minimum required tree caliper per lot (60"/40"/30") that makes clearing the yard illegal. On a 6,000 sq ft R-2 lot that already has a house, a drive and a deck, that cap IS the conversation. So the page opens by being the site that actually answers it — the district-by-district table, the tree requirement, the Building & Zoning number, and a straight statement of whether the town counts turf as impervious (go ask, then publish it). Second beat: SALT. Retirees at a median age of 57.5, one in three over 65, tired of watering grass that salt spray keeps killing on a postage-stamp lot. Third beat, a different customer entirely: R-3 is named 'High Density/WEEKLY RENTAL' in the town's own zoning — absentee owners buying maintenance certainty for a property they visit twice a year, in a town whose median build year is 1986 and whose nickname is 'The Family Beach.' WHY THIS DIFFERS FROM ITS NEIGHBOURS: Longs, 20 miles inland, is big cheap lots, four golf courses, no municipality and no permit — the freedom page. Forestbrook is standing water and a flood-mitigation grant — the drainage page. Murrells Inlet next door is the fishing-village-turned-restaurant-row page. Surfside is the only one whose lead is a regulation and a chemistry problem: a hard percentage in the town code, and salt. Nothing about flooding, nothing about acreage, nothing about HOA approval — this town's rules come from Town Hall, not a board.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: THE ONLY INCORPORATED TOWN IN THIS BATCH, and it publishes hard numbers (Town of Surfside Beach District Regulations, updated 02/08/2022). MAXIMUM IMPERVIOUS COVERAGE: R-1 Low Density Residential 40%; R-2 Medium Density 45%; R-3 High Density/Weekly Rental 50%. MAXIMUM LOT COVERAGE: R-1 30%, R-2 30%, R-3 40%. REQUIRED TREES PER LOT: R-1 five trees, 60 inches total caliper measured 2 ft from ground; R-2 five trees, 40 inches total; R-3 three trees, 30 inches total — so you cannot clear-and-turf a Surfside lot; the tree minimum is written into the district table. Setbacks: R-1 25/20/10 ft, R-2 25/20/10, R-3 20/15/5. Max height 35 ft (R-1/R-2), 55 ft (R-3). C-1 commercial: min lot 10,000 sq ft on Hwy 17, 75 ft front setback; C-2 Central Business has no setbacks or minimum lot. Note R-3 is literally NAMED 'High Density/WEEKLY RENTAL' — the town zones for weekly rentals by district, which supports an entire rental-owner section. Building & Zoning: 843-913-6111 (the same PDF prints 843-913-6341 on page 2 — call and confirm which is current before publishing a number). CRITICAL UNRESOLVED QUESTION that should become the page's own stated question: the district regulations do NOT define whether artificial turf counts toward impervious coverage. Municode blocked automated access this session. Ask Building & Zoning directly and publish the answer — being the only turf site on the Grand Strand that actually asked the town is worth more than any amount of copy. WARNING FOR WHOEVER WRITES THIS PAGE: searching 'Surfside Beach synthetic turf ordinance' surfaces Ordinance No. 2023-1749 from the TOWN OF SURFSIDE, FLORIDA. Different municipality, different state. Do not cite it.
facts.turf_specifics: Coastal, minimal elevation, roughly 2.0 sq mi directly on the Atlantic. Three constraints unique to this page: (1) SALT — persistent salt spray and salt-laden rain, which kills the maintenance case for natural turf and raises a legitimate durability question about infill, backing and UV/salt resistance; answer it head-on. (2) SAND — near-beach lots are essentially free-draining sand, so the Forestbrook drainage sermon is the WRONG pitch here; the base problem is stability and settlement, not percolation. (3) LOT SIZE against a CODIFIED IMPERVIOUS CAP — on a 6,000 sq ft R-2 lot that already has a house, driveway and deck, the arithmetic is tight, and how the town classifies artificial turf decides whether the job is permittable at all. Also: the town's beach-management provisions restrict vegetation between the landward trough of the primary oceanfront dune and the shore protection line to selected non-native vegetation 'but not to include nonnative grass turf or covering' — i.e. do NOT install turf in the dune zone. That is a real seaward-lot limit worth naming honestly; Municode returned 403 to automated access this session, so verify the exact chapter and section before quoting it.
facts.housing_stock: Checked 2026-09-07. Median year built 1986 — a 1970s–80s beach town, not new construction. 4,272 housing units across roughly 2.0 sq mi. Of 1,994 OCCUPIED units, 64.99% owner-occupied and 35.01% renter — but note the gap between 4,272 units and 1,994 occupied households: a very large share is seasonal/vacation and non-resident-owned, and the town's own description acknowledges substantial vacation-rental property owned by non-residents. Median value of a home with a mortgage $416,300. Lots are SMALL and legally capped: R-1 minimum 9,000 sq ft / 75 ft width; R-2 minimum 6,000 sq ft / 60 ft; R-3 minimum 3,600 sq ft detached, 3,000 sq ft attached, 30 ft width. Typology runs from original single-storey beach cottages and raised piling houses near the ocean to duplexes and attached product in R-3, plus condo. HOA prevalence INSIDE the town limits is LOW relative to the batch — Surfside is an old platted grid town, so the binding rules are the TOWN's, not a board's. That inversion is the whole point of this page.
facts.who_lives_there: Median age 57.5; roughly one-third of residents 65+; 2020 census population 4,155 (up from 3,837 in 2010). Median household income $74,202, average $88,453. 91.99% white. Ranked #4 Best Places to Retire in South Carolina. 57% of residents 15+ are married; 27% have children under 18. So three populations: a retiree core, a genuine family-vacation visitor economy on top of it (the town's own nickname is 'The Family Beach'), and a third group that never appears in the census — absentee weekly-rental owners making maintenance decisions from another state. That third group is the best residential customer in this batch: they pay for labour they cannot supervise.

That is the named in-town course. Blackmoor Golf Club in Murrells Inlet is the other likely neighbour — NOT verified this session, confirm before naming. Two revenue lines: (a) the park's own amenity surfaces — Sandy Harbor Family Fun Center including mini-golf, the DOG PARK, the skate park, Camptown Center, Recreation Building; and (b) 2,579 individual annual leaseholders each with a small sandy patch around a park model — a referral engine, not a single job. SURFSIDE BEACH BARK PARK (town-owned, licence-tag gated — a small, winnable municipal pet-turf demonstrator). FULLER PARK (two lighted tennis courts, playground — safety surfacing). ALL CHILDREN'S PARK. DEER TRACK GOLF RESORT (two 18s). The Highway 17 / Surfside Drive commercial strip (C-1 through C-4, min lots 3,000–10,000 sq ft — small-footprint storefronts, patios, putting attractions). Regional proof points the owner can cite in any pitch: GRAND PARK ATHLETIC COMPLEX at Market Common, Myrtle Beach — the Styers Athletic Complex there completed a full renovation of all nine multipurpose fields in February with new turf including around the pitching mound and home plate; seven large multipurpose fields plus two youth fields, all synthetic, all lit. DOUG SHAW MEMORIAL STADIUM, Myrtle Beach — FieldTurf, $5.4M renovation in 2017. NOT VERIFIED: named daycares and pet daycares inside the town limits, and the Horry County elementary school serving Surfside (Seaside Elementary is likely but unconfirmed) — verify before naming.
facts.landmarks: The Surfside Beach Fishing Pier — town-owned, 814 ft, free to enter, with an elevator and walking ramp. 'The Family Beach' — the town's actual nickname, on its own signage. Fuller Park at Surfside Drive and Myrtle Drive: two lighted tennis courts, playground, picnic area, restrooms, next to the Horry County Memorial Library branch. The Surfside Beach Bark Park (near the library and pier) — dogs must wear a Surfside Beach licence tag, $10 for locals at Town Hall. All Children's Park. Incorporated 1964; previously Roach's Beach, then Floral Beach, renamed Surfside Beach c. 1952; the 18th-century plantation on the site was 'The Ark,' about 3,200 acres. On 4 February 2023 the Chinese surveillance balloon was shot down directly off this town's coast — a genuine, dateable local reference no template page will have. Ocean Lakes Family Campground sits immediately north at 6001 S Kings Hwy (29575). Garden City Beach immediately south.

name: Nixons Crossroads

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH: the yard that has to look good while you are not in it. Nixons Crossroads is a four-highway junction, not a village — US 17, SC 9, SC 90 and Sea Mountain Highway all meet here — and the tract around it is 19.2% vacant and 12.3% seasonally occupied with a surrounding CDP median age of 60.1. Half your prospects leave in April or arrive in October. Pair that with the physical facts nowhere else in this batch has: Blanton sand with a sixty-inch water table that lets irrigation and fertiliser leach straight through, the Atlantic Intracoastal Waterway half a mile away at the USGS tidal gauge literally named for this crossroads, and the ocean under three miles off. So: no irrigation to run while you are north, no service to schedule, no salt-burned brown patches when you come back, and a villa courtyard putting green for a retiree with five courses inside two miles — Eagle Nest, River Hills, Surf Golf & Beach Club, The Valley at Eastport, Tidewater. And the POA-submission service as the conversion hook, because almost every prospect here is inside an association. WHY IT DIFFERS FROM THE NEIGHBOURS: Little River proper is the waterfront fishing village with the Blue Crab Festival and the seafood houses; Cherry Grove is oceanfront rental; Nixons Crossroads is the SERVICE JUNCTION behind both — the hospital, the Walmart, the four schools, the pet stores, and the villa POAs. Write it as the crossroads page, not another beach page: the place everyone in the north end drives through, where the golf villas and the retail and the fields actually are.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: The critical distinction on this page is jurisdictional: Nixons Crossroads straddles the boundary between the City of North Myrtle Beach and unincorporated Horry County, and neighbouring properties can fall on either side. Horry County framework (VERIFIED): stormwater permit at 0.5 acre of land disturbance with single-family residential construction exempt; ordinance effective Oct 1 2000, re-enacted July 2017; proposed 15-ft wetland buffer landscape ordinance with first reading scheduled 21 April 2026. City of North Myrtle Beach has its own zoning, landscape and stormwater code which I could NOT retrieve this session — flag it, and have the client confirm before the page claims anything about city rules. THE OPERATIVE RULE FOR MOST CUSTOMERS HERE IS THE POA/HOA DECLARATION, not the government: the villa and golf-community associations listed above typically control front-yard ground cover, exterior alterations, courtyard and patio surfaces, and fence material and height. A page that leads with 'we prepare the POA architectural-review submission for you' will out-convert one that leads with product. HONEST GAP: no specific declaration was readable this session, and horrycountysc.gov was unreachable on 2026-09-07.
facts.turf_specifics: VERIFIED point soil (USDA NRCS SSURGO, queried 2026-09-07 at 33.8577/-78.6603): map unit 130136, Blanton sand, 0 to 6 percent slopes — 85% Blanton, moderately well drained, hydrologic group A (NOT the A/D or B/D dual rating the other three carry), Loamy siliceous semiactive thermic Grossarenic Paleudults; minor Osier 3% (poorly drained). Minimum annual depth to water table: 152 cm (~60 inches). Flooding: none. This is the mirror image of Goretown: 'Grossarenic' means the sandy epipedon runs roughly 40–80 inches deep, so the water table sits five feet down and infiltration is excessively fast. The Nixons Crossroads problem is NOT perched water — it is that nothing holds. Natural turf here needs constant irrigation and constant feeding, and nutrients leach straight through; a synthetic base needs compaction and confinement discipline rather than heroic drainage. SALT: this is the only genuinely salt-exposed place in the batch. The USGS operates gauge 02110777, 'AIW at Highway 9 at Nixons Crossroads', a TIDAL STREAM site at 33.85156/-78.65585, roughly half a mile from the crossroads, in service since 1986 — the Atlantic Intracoastal Waterway runs right past. Cherry Grove's oceanfront is about 2.5–3 miles away. Salt aerosol, brackish irrigation risk in some wells, and UV load are all real design inputs here and nowhere else in this batch.
facts.housing_stock: The best-documented of the four. Verified location 33.8577, -78.6603, ZIP 29566, elevation 51 ft — the junction of US 17, SC 9, SC 90 and Sea Mountain Highway (S-26-20) in Little River, with SC 31 (Carolina Bays Parkway) 1.8 mi away and Robert Edge Parkway 2.1 mi. NeighborhoodScout's Nixons Crossroads tract: median home price $346,730 (above 60% of SC neighbourhoods), median rent $1,863; housing is 'primarily medium to large single-family homes and mobile homes', most built after 2000 or between 1970 and 1999; VACANCY 19.2% — higher than 87.3% of all US neighbourhoods — and 12.3% of housing is seasonally occupied. The surrounding Little River CDP had 11,711 residents at the 2020 census, up from 7,027 in 2000. OSM shows what that vacancy actually is: a dense mat of golf-villa and condo POAs inside two miles — Golf Colony, Golf Colony Resort, Golf View Plantation, Lightkeepers Village, Robbers Roost Villas, Bay Tree and Village at Bay Tree, Cedar Creek Village, Club Villas, Harbour Front Villas, Coquina Harbour, Plantation Harbour, Carolina Yacht Landing, Paradise Island, Portside Village, Sawgrass Village, Sunset Village — alongside newer single-family: Seabrook Plantation, Tybre Downs, Bellacroft, Seaglass Village, Hiddenbrooke, Princeton Place, Bridgeway Park, Bay Forest, Palmetto Shores. This is the most HOA/POA-saturated place in the batch by a wide margin.

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH SALT, MARSH AND AN OWNER WHO ISN'T THERE. Seaside is the only town in this batch that is genuinely coastal, and the soil data proves it rather than asserting it: it is the only one whose ground returns Kureb and Newhan (excessively drained dune and DREDGED sand), Wando, Pactolus — and Bohicket silty clay loam, a Typic Sulfaquent, which is tidal salt marsh. At 14.8 ft it sits roughly 20 to 29 feet below its neighbours. The water table runs about 60 inches down on the Wando ridge and sits at the surface in the Bohicket marsh, sometimes within one property line. So the page leads with the two coastal failure modes natural grass cannot beat here — salt burn from aerosol and brackish groundwater, and sand that either drains so fast nothing survives or is marsh that never drains at all — and positions turf as the only surface indifferent to both. The second half of the lead is the demographic, and it is stronger here than anywhere: median age 68, 53.7% of homes vacant, 38.9% seasonal. Half these houses are dark right now. Nobody is flying down from Pennsylvania to water a lawn. Turf that looks the same in February as in July, with no irrigation, no fertiliser and no service call, is a product built for an absentee owner in their late sixties. WHY THIS DIFFERS FROM ITS NEIGHBOURS: Grissettown, only 4.8 miles up the SAME NC 904, is 29 feet higher and sits on Goldsboro loam — its problem is a dense subsoil that holds water and its page is about building putting greens for a wealthier, more year-round golf buyer. Thomasboro's people are actually home 81% of the time and its ground is uniform wet flatwoods. Civietown is inland, has no golf and no salt. Seaside is the only page that gets to talk about tidal marsh, dredged sand, CAMA Estuarine Shoreline and Ocean Hazard AECs, and the $119 minor CAMA permit — and it should, because that regulatory literacy is what a waterfront second-home owner is actually buying.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: JURISDICTION WARNING for this page: Seaside is unincorporated, but it sits immediately against the Town of Sunset Beach (planning & zoning, and stormwater, at 910-579-6297) and the town maintains its own Unified Development Ordinance and Code of Ordinances — so which rulebook applies is parcel-specific and must be confirmed, not assumed. On unincorporated parcels the Brunswick County UDO applies, including its Impervious Surface definition, which names 'compacted earth (such as marl and coquina), gravel, concrete, asphalt' as impervious and 'porous pavement, uncovered wooden slatted decks and the water area of a swimming pool' as pervious — artificial turf unnamed. The genuinely Seaside-specific layer is CAMA: Brunswick County Planning issues Minor CAMA Permits (application fee $119, payable to Brunswick County Planning) and the Areas of Environmental Concern that apply here are the Estuarine Shoreline AEC — which requires structural footprint documentation and wetland delineation — and the Ocean Hazard Area, which requires dune mapping, vegetation-line location and setback calculation. Any turf work near the marsh edge or the waterway can land in an AEC. The county UDO also designates the Intracoastal Waterway, from the New Hanover County line to the South Carolina state line, as a Viewshed Protection Overlay applying within 300 ft of normal high water. HOA GAP: Sea Trail and Oyster Bay covenant/ARB language on artificial turf was not retrievable publicly — pull the CC&Rs.
facts.turf_specifics: THIS IS THE FIELD THAT SEPARATES SEASIDE FROM EVERY OTHER TOWN IN THE BATCH. USGS elevation 14.8 ft — roughly 20 to 29 feet LOWER than the other three. USDA SSURGO at the centroid: Wando fine sand, 0 to 6 percent slopes (85% Wando, WELL DRAINED, a Typic Quartzipsamment; 3% Leon, poorly drained and hydric; 2% Muckalee, poorly drained and hydric). Within a ~1.2 km box Seaside is the ONLY one of the four to return true coastal soils: Kureb fine sand 1–8% (EXCESSIVELY drained, Spodic Quartzipsamment), Newhan fine sand DREDGED 2–30% (excessively drained — literally spoil material), Pactolus fine sand, Wando fine sand — AND Bohicket silty clay loam, which is a Typic Sulfaquent: very poorly drained tidal salt marsh with potential acid sulfate conditions. Plus Leon fine sand (Aeric Alaquod — a spodosol with a cemented spodic horizon that perches water above it) and Torhunta mucky fine sandy loam. SSURGO seasonal high water table for NC019: Wando about 60 inches, Bohicket and Torhunta at the SURFACE, Leon within about 6 inches. So on a single Seaside street the water table can be five feet down on the dune ridge and at grade in the marsh edge fifty yards away, and the sand can go from excessively drained (Kureb/Newhan drains so fast nothing holds) to a sulfaquent muck. Salt exposure is the other differentiator and it is real here in a way it is not at Thomasboro or Civietown: Seaside is ~2.0 mi from the Sunset Beach Fishing Pier and sits directly behind the Intracoastal Waterway and salt marsh, so aerosol salt load, brackish groundwater and salt-burned natural turf are ordinary conditions.
facts.housing_stock: RESEARCH FLAG: no census place, no population figure, no town government — OSM 'hamlet' only. Proxy ZCTA 28468 (Sunset Beach), which is dominated by the island and Sea Trail. ACS 2023 5-yr for 28468: 5,707 housing units but only 2,642 occupied — 53.7% VACANT, the emptiest ZIP in the batch. 2,218 units (38.9% of all stock) are seasonal/recreational/occasional. Median year built 1999, median home value $412,000, owner occupancy 87.4% of occupied units. Housing type on the ground splits three ways: Sea Trail's late-1980s–1990s golf villas and patio homes, 1990s–2000s single-family on the mainland side of the bridge, and older/modest frontage at the actual NC 179 / NC 904 crossroads. County UDO Table 4-1 lot minimums apply on unincorporated parcels (7,500 sf in R-7500 with utilities, 6,000 sf in R-6000/SBR-6000), but much of the surrounding development is inside Sunset Beach town limits or its ETJ — a page for Seaside MUST say the jurisdiction line runs through this area and get confirmed parcel by parcel. HOA-heavy: Sea Trail and Oyster Bay are covenant-governed communities.
facts.who_lives_there: Median age 68.0 in ZCTA 28468 — the OLDEST in this batch and one of the oldest ZIPs in North Carolina. Combined with 53.7% vacancy and 38.9% seasonal use, the profile is unmistakable: retirees and second-home owners, more than half the houses dark at any given moment, and the occupied ones held by people in their late sixties and up. Practically, that means a large share of your prospects are absentee for months at a time, are not going to run an irrigation system from Ohio or Pennsylvania, and are actively looking for a yard that survives neglect. It also means the buying decision often runs through a property manager or a rental company rather than the owner standing in the driveway.
facts.golf: Seaside is the closest of the four to Sea Trail Golf Links (1.3 mi) — three courses, designed by Willard Byrd, Dan Maples and Rees Jones, in Sunset Beach. Also verified: Oyster Bay Golf Links (Legends) 2.6 mi, Ocean Ridge Plantation 2.6 mi (Tiger's Eye, Leopard's Chase, Panther's Run, Lion's Paw), Thistle Golf Club 3.3 mi, Brunswick Plantation 5.5 mi, Crow Creek 5.6 mi. The commercial book here is resort and HOA amenity work: Sea Trail and Oyster Bay practice greens, clubhouse and pool-deck landscape turf, rental-property front yards, and vacation-rental management companies as a channel. name: Conway

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH WATER — NOT SALT, NOT GOLF, NOT TOURISTS. Conway is the inverse of the beach towns and the page has to say so in the first sentence. Fourteen miles inland at 16 feet of elevation, on a river that crested above 21 feet in 2018 and beat the 2016 record by three feet, in a city where the three most common soils — Meggett, Eulonia and Wahee, together about 42% of the ground — are every one of them described as slow permeability and poorly to moderately drained. That is the opposite problem from North Myrtle Beach's excessively drained dune sand, and it makes Conway the engineered-base page: what goes UNDER the turf, how deep the drainage aggregate runs, where the outlet is, and why a turf lawn here is a drainage job that happens to end in green fibre. Back it with the one thing no competitor can borrow — the teal Shaw Sports field at Brooks Stadium, installed 2015, three miles from downtown, the most photographed artificial turf in the state. Then pitch to who actually lives here: median age 30.4, 12.1% vacancy, young working families and CCU staff in the house twelve months a year, whose complaint is a back yard that is mud from October to March and whose kids and dogs are the reason. Deliberately different from North Myrtle Beach (a permit-compliance page for absentee retirees), from Myrtle Beach (a municipal-fields pitch), and from Carolina Forest (an HOA-approval page). Conway is the only one of the four where the honest lead is 'we fix drainage.'
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: Conway operates under a Unified Development Ordinance and a Flood Damage Prevention Ordinance; the UDO and Code of Ordinances were amended to adopt all flood maps including Hurricane Matthew levels, and require building area to be elevated at least 2 feet above the 100-year flood elevation. FEMA distributed a Flood Insurance Study (45051CV003B) in September 2015 and revised it after the 2016 flooding. As an NFIP participant Conway must issue permits for ALL development in the 100-year floodplain, and 'development' is defined broadly to include any man-made change to the land — which on its face reaches a turf installation with an imported aggregate base on a floodplain lot. Proposed development must not increase flooding or create a dangerous situation for adjacent property owners. RESEARCH GAP: cityofconway.com returned 403 to every attempt on 2026-09-07, so I could not read the UDO's landscaping, lot-coverage or fence provisions directly, and I found no Conway ordinance that names artificial turf. Verify before the page makes a compliance claim. The historic district almost certainly carries design review over street-facing changes — worth confirming with the city, because 'we do the back yard, not the streetscape' is a useful thing to be able to say in Conway. Statewide: SC Code § 27-30-130 — HOA rules must be recorded and re-recorded annually by January 10 with the Horry County Register of Deeds to be enforceable.
facts.turf_specifics: THE SLOWEST-DRAINING GROUND IN THE BATCH, AND THE ONLY REAL RIVER-FLOOD EXPOSURE. Conway's own Natural Resources element counts approximately 26 soil types in the city, and the three most common are all slow: Meggett loam at ~17% (Southern Coastal Plain / Atlantic Coast Flatwoods / Tidewater; POORLY draining; flooding none to frequent for brief to long periods; permeability SLOW); Eulonia loamy fine sand at 12.6% (drains moderately well; permeability SLOW); Wahee fine sandy loam at 12% (drains somewhat poorly; permeability SLOW). Nearly half the city sits on soils that will not take water at the rate a turf base needs to shed it. On top of that: approximately 24% of Horry County's total land area is 100-year floodplain; Conway has non-tidal floodplains along the Waccamaw with AE and A1-30 zones; and the city's Unified Development Ordinance requires building area to be at or elevated to at least 2 feet above the 100-year flood elevation. The Waccamaw crested just above 21 feet after Hurricane Florence in 2018, breaking the 17.9-foot Hurricane Matthew record of 2016 by more than three feet and inundating close to 1,000 homes near Conway; the city ran a voluntary buyout programme (43 owners in process before Florence, 32 more added after). Kingston Lake and Crabtree Canal drain into the same system, and Crabtree Swamp has been through a floodplain-restoration project. Salt exposure: effectively none, 14 miles inland — this is a freshwater, tannic blackwater environment. Practical turf spec: engineered base with positive fall to a designed outlet, generous drainage aggregate depth, and a written answer to 'where does the water actually go' on every quote.
facts.housing_stock: 2020 census: 24,849 residents, 8,277 households, 9,421 housing units, 12.1% vacant — the lowest vacancy in the batch and a fraction of North Myrtle Beach's 62.6%. Average home built 1993. About 45% own outright, ~26% rent. City area 25.41 sq mi, elevation 16 ft, on the west bank of the Waccamaw River about 14 miles inland. The stock is genuinely layered and nothing like the beach towns: a National Register downtown historic district (listed 19 August 1994, roughly bounded by Fourth Avenue, Kingston Street, Third Avenue and Laurel Street) with antebellum and Victorian houses under enormous live oaks, including City Hall / the Old Horry County Courthouse designed by Robert Mills; then mid-century in-town neighbourhoods; then 1990s–2020s subdivisions spreading toward Highway 501 and Coastal Carolina University; plus a large student-rental sector. Lot sizes in the older sections are big and irregular; the newer 501-corridor subdivisions are HOA-governed and conventional.
facts.who_lives_there: Median age 30.4 — by far the youngest in the batch and 32 years younger than North Myrtle Beach. That is Coastal Carolina University plus young working families. 41.2% of households are married couples and 34.5% are female-headed without a spouse present. Historic median household income figures for the city run well below the coastal towns and poverty is meaningfully higher. This is a year-round, working, county-seat town — courthouse, Conway Medical Center, school district and university employment — not a resort and not a retirement colony. The buyer here is price-sensitive, lives in the house all twelve months, and is far more likely to be motivated by a yard that stops turning to mud than by aesthetics.
facts.golf: Verified in Conway: Shaftesbury Glen Golf & Fish Club, 951 Shaftesbury Ln, Conway 29526 — 18 holes in an English manor style, 4-star Golf Digest 'Places To Play', named Golf Course of the Year by the Myrtle Beach Area Golf Course Owners Association. The Hackler Course at Coastal Carolina University (the university's own course, listed by Visit Myrtle Beach). Wild Wing Plantation and Burning Ridge are both Conway-area courses on the 501 corridor and Aberdeen Country Club is just north toward Longs — all three are locally well known but I could NOT verify their addresses by direct fetch on 2026-09-07 (Wild Wing's site failed on TLS), so confirm before publishing. Myrtle Beach National's three courses sit on 501 between Conway and Carolina Forest and are claimed by both.
facts.commercial_targets:
COASTAL CAROLINA UNIVERSITY IS THE ANCHOR AND IT IS ALREADY A TURF CUSTOMER. Brooks Stadium plays on Shaw Sports PowerBlade artificial turf in TEAL, installed in 2015 (natural grass 2003–2014), capacity 21,000 — it is one of the very few non-traditional-coloured college football fields in the country and it is nationally recognisable. Springs Brooks Stadium is CCU baseball (2016 national champions). CCU also has soccer, lacrosse and softball venues and the Hackler Course. A turf company that can say 'the most recognisable synthetic field in South Carolina is three miles from downtown Conway' has all the local proof it will ever need — and every field CCU owns is on a replacement cycle.
Other targets: Conway High School (Tigers), Conway Middle, Whittemore Park Middle, and the Conway-area elementary schools, all Horry County Schools; the City of Conway Parks & Recreation ball fields (inventory unverified — cityofconway.com blocked); Conway Medical Center campus grounds; the downtown Riverwalk and Main Street streetscape planters; and the Highway 501 commercial corridor. PET/CHILDCARE: I could not verify named doggy daycares or childcare centres inside Conway — the business directories blocked retrieval on 2026-09-07. Do not invent names; walk the 501 corridor or pull the SC DSS licensed-facility list before this section of the page is written.
facts.landmarks: The Conway Riverwalk along the Waccamaw and the Conway Marina. The Old Horry County Courthouse / City Hall (1825, designed by Robert Mills, architect of the Washington Monument). The Conway Downtown Historic District, 5.15 acres, on the National Register since 19 August 1994. The live oaks over the downtown streets — Conway is a Preserve America community and famously routes streets around its oaks. Kingston Lake. Crabtree Canal and the restored Crabtree Swamp floodplain. Coastal Carolina University. Conway Medical Center. Theatre of the Republic. The Horry County Museum. The city was founded in 1732 as Kingston, then Conwayborough, and has been Conway since 1883.

name: Carolina Shores

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH THE ARCHITECTURAL REVIEW COMMITTEE, NOT THE LAWN. Carolina Shores is the batch's pure inland HOA retirement town — no beach, no river, no tourists, no school, no seafood, 53.5% over 65, tripled in twenty years, and made up of eight named covenanted subdivisions packed into 2.88 square miles. It is the one town here where the person who can say no to your project is a volunteer neighbour on an ARC board, not a town planner and not a state coastal regulator. So the page should open on approvals, not on grass: 'We prepare the submittal your architectural review committee actually wants — product spec, infill, drainage plan, colour and pile height, and a site sketch — and we've done it in Calabash Lakes, Eagle Run and The Farm at Brunswick.' Everything else follows from the demographics: turf as the answer to not wanting to mow at 70, and pet turf for a dog-heavy retiree population with no children. Why this differs from its neighbours: Sunset Beach's gatekeeper is a state-driven coastal code with hard numeric impervious caps and a PE certification path; Calabash's customer is a restaurant, not a homeowner; Shallotte's customer is a working family and a school. Carolina Shores' gatekeeper is private covenant law. Use the 1998 secession from Calabash — over sewer, garbage and sign rules — as the proof-of-local-knowledge hook; it explains, in one sentence, why this town is defined by rules and why the boundaries with Calabash interlock so confusingly. Do NOT reuse the beach-town 'salt and storms' angle here: this town has no waterfront, and saying otherwise will read as a template to anyone who lives there.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: HONEST GAP — THE MOST IMPORTANT ONE IN THIS BATCH. The Town of Carolina Shores publishes its code through American Legal (codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/carolinashores), and every route I tried was blocked by a Cloudflare bot challenge that I did not attempt to defeat. I therefore have NO verified text on Carolina Shores' impervious surface limits, stormwater thresholds, fence rules, or landscaping standards, and I will not invent them. What IS verified from the town's own site: a Planning & Zoning division sits under Public Works alongside Inspections and Code Compliance; there is a Planning Board that reviews development applications, plus an Economic Development Commission and a Parks Commission; the town runs a Flood Map Modernization programme with a resident learning guide; and there is a specific Golf Cart Ordinance governing golf cart operation within town limits — a small but genuinely local detail. Town offices are at 200 Persimmon Road. THE REAL RULE-MAKER HERE IS PRIVATE, NOT PUBLIC. With eight named covenanted subdivisions inside 2.88 square miles and 53.5% of residents over 65, the binding constraint on a turf job in Carolina Shores is almost certainly the subdivision's architectural review committee and its CC&Rs, not the town code. I could not retrieve any subdivision's covenant text this session (the expected POA domain does not resolve). ACTION BEFORE PUBLISHING: pull the American Legal code in a normal browser, and pull the CC&Rs / ARC application for at least Carolina Shores Subdivision, Calabash Lakes and The Farm at Brunswick — those three will carry the page.
facts.turf_specifics: Inland mainland flatwoods — the driest, most conventional installation environment in this batch, and worth saying so. No oceanfront, no barrier island dune sand, no CAMA Area of Environmental Concern, and negligible direct salt spray, because the town has no significant water frontage at all. The regional soil pattern is the poorly drained Leon-type coastal flatwoods profile: a spodic Bh hardpan within 30 inches of the surface, seasonal high water table at 6–18 inches for several months a year, and moderate-to-moderately-slow permeability through the pan. That is the governing constraint here — flat, low-relief subdivision lots on a hardpan, where water does not go down and there is very little natural fall to send it sideways. Turf base design needs a designed outlet, and on these tight platted lots that usually means tying into the subdivision's existing stormwater conveyance, which is an HOA conversation as much as an engineering one. The town also runs a 'Flood Map Modernization' initiative, so flood-zone designations are actively being revised and should be checked per address. CAVEAT: soil series is a regional pattern from USDA Official Series Descriptions, not verified parcel-level mapping for Carolina Shores.
facts.housing_stock: 2,767 housing units, 15.8% vacancy — the middle of this batch, and the signature of a town that is mostly primary-residence retirement rather than either working-family (Shallotte, 6.8%) or vacation-rental (Sunset Beach, 55.1%). 2,331 households, nearly 58% married-couple, 25.1% female householder with no spouse or partner present. Median age 66.0; 53.5% of residents are 65 or older; only 7.4% under 18. Population 4,588 in 2020, up from 1,482 in 2000 — it TRIPLED in twenty years, which means the stock is overwhelmingly late-1990s through 2010s platted subdivision product, built new for retirees, on a compact 2.88 sq mi. This is the most HOA-saturated town in the batch: the town itself lists eight named subdivisions — Beacon Townes, Calabash Lakes, Carolina Shores Subdivision, Eagle Run, Lighthouse Cove, The Farm at Brunswick, The Village at Calabash, and River Rock at Shingletree — and a town of 2.88 square miles that is essentially a stack of named, covenanted subdivisions is a town where the architectural review committee, not the town planner, is the real gatekeeper. NOTE: typical lot dimensions and per-subdivision HOA covenant text were NOT verified this session.
facts.who_lives_there: Retirees, and specifically inland retirees who chose NOT to pay for water. 53.5% over 65 is the second-highest share in the batch, and with only 7.4% under 18 there is effectively no family population. Unlike Sunset Beach these are primary residences occupied most of the year (15.8% vacancy, not 55%), and unlike Calabash there is no tourist economy layered on top. The town has no beach, no river frontage, no school, and no restaurant row — despite its name, 'the town lacks waterfront access to any significant body of water,' the name having come from a country club rather than any shore. Residents drive to Calabash to eat, to Sunset Beach or Ocean Isle for sand, and to Myrtle Beach (24 miles southwest) or Shallotte for everything else.
facts.golf: The town is literally named after a country club, and Carolina Shores Golf & Country Club is the course associated with it — BUT I could not verify its current operating status from any primary source this session (the expected domain does not resolve), and courses in this corridor have closed and reopened. VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING. What is confirmed is that Carolina Shores is ringed by verified courses within a few minutes, essentially all of them across the interlocked boundary in Calabash: Brunswick Plantation & Golf Resort (380 Brunswick Drive NW, Calabash, 27 holes — Azalea, Dogwood, Magnolia — by Byrd and Johnson); The Pearl Golf Links (1300 Pearl Blvd, Calabash, Dan Maples, 1987); Meadowlands Golf Club (Hickman Crossroads, Willard Byrd and David Johnson); and Farmstead Golf Links, less than a mile from Meadowlands. Also unverified but commonly cited nearby: Crow Creek Golf Club (Calabash).
facts.commercial_targets: THIN, AND WORTH SAYING SO. Carolina Shores has no school, no sports complex, and no restaurant row — those are in Shallotte and Calabash respectively. The realistic commercial inventory is: the town's own park facilities (a Parks Commission exists and sets seasonal park hours), the town Recycle Center and Town Hall grounds at 200 Persimmon Road, and — the substantive one — the eight subdivision HOAs themselves as institutional buyers for common areas, entry monuments, clubhouse surrounds and amenity lawns. An HOA common-area contract in a 53.5%-over-65 subdivision is a better-fit commercial target here than any daycare or ballfield. Immediately adjacent across the interlocked Calabash line: Brunswick Plantation & Golf Resort (resort grounds and villa common areas). GAP: no named daycare, pet daycare, boarding or grooming business was verified for Carolina Shores; the session's web search budget was exhausted. Given the demographics, pet boarding and veterinary rather than child daycare is the likelier fit and should be searched specifically.
facts.landmarks: Town Hall at 200 Persimmon Road. The eight named subdivisions are themselves the landmarks locals navigate by: Beacon Townes, Calabash Lakes, Carolina Shores Subdivision, Eagle Run, Lighthouse Cove, The Farm at Brunswick, The Village at Calabash, River Rock at Shingletree. US 17 runs northwest through town; Wilmington is 47 miles northeast and Myrtle Beach 24 miles southwest. The town operates a Recycle Center and town park facilities with seasonal hours. facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH: the two-year-old house whose builder sod already failed in the back corner. Nixonville is not a golf page and not a retiree page — it is the SC 90 boom corridor, the lowest and loamiest ground of the four, and the only one of the four whose defining problem is new construction on wet soil. The specifics that make it undeniable: 3,243 approved-but-unbuilt units on this stretch as of January 2021; traffic up from 6,100 to 14,400 vehicles a day in a decade; Horry County Schools paying $6.3M for 61 acres on Highway 90 in March 2026 because there is no school out here; Yauhannah fine sandy loam rated hydrologic group B/D with Bladen C/D clay inclusions and an 18-inch seasonal water table, under whatever compaction the builder's equipment left. So the products are pet turf and kid play areas and fixing the wet corner — a dog run that stops being mud in February, a play surface under the swing set, a rear yard the HOA architectural committee will approve. WHY IT DIFFERS FROM THE NEIGHBOURS: Carolina Forest six miles south is 1990s–2000s master-planned and mature — its lawns are thirty years old and its trees are grown; Nixonville is the raw 2018-2026 edge of the same wave on wetter, heavier ground with no school, no shade and no established landscaping. Nixons Crossroads twenty miles east is retirees and villas. Nixonville is strollers and dogs.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: Same county framework as Allen (VERIFIED): stormwater permit required at 0.5 acre of land disturbance, single-family residential construction exempt; Horry County Stormwater Ordinance effective Oct 1 2000, re-enacted July 2017. VERIFIED (pending): proposed county landscape ordinance requiring a 15-ft buffer from all wetlands, first reading scheduled 21 April 2026 after deferral from 17 March 2026 — this one matters more in Nixonville than anywhere else in the batch, because Tilly Swamp and the Waccamaw wetlands run through the subdivisions and by comparison Bluffton requires 50 ft and Georgetown County has proposed 35 ft plus a 15-ft setback. THE REAL RULE THAT BITES HERE IS PRIVATE, NOT PUBLIC: every one of the named subdivisions above will have a recorded declaration of covenants with an architectural review committee, and in new Horry County builder communities those routinely govern rear-yard surfaces, fence height and material, and drainage alteration. facts.turf_specifics: VERIFIED point soil (USDA NRCS SSURGO, queried 2026-09-07 at 33.8350/-78.8850): map unit 130174, Yauhannah fine sandy loam, 0 to 2 percent slopes — 90% Yauhannah, moderately well drained, hydrologic group B/D, Fine-loamy siliceous semiactive thermic Aquic Hapludults. Minor components: Ogeechee 2% (poorly drained, B/D) and Bladen 2% (poorly drained, hydrologic group C/D, Fine mixed semiactive thermic Typic Albaquults — i.e. clayey and genuinely slow). Minimum annual depth to water table: 46 cm (~18 inches). Flooding: None at the crossroads; ponding: none. Elevation 23 ft — the LOWEST of these four places. This is the key technical differentiator: Nixonville is the only one of the four on a fine sandy LOAM rather than a sand. It is loamier, it infiltrates more slowly than Blanton or Leon sand, it holds a B/D rating, and it carries Bladen clay inclusions rated C/D. Layer that under builder compaction from heavy equipment on a two-year-old lot and you get exactly the complaint the corridor is famous for: standing water in the back corner, sod that dies in the low spot, mud where the dog turns and where the swing set sits. Salt exposure: minimal — roughly 9–10 miles inland. The Waccamaw River is 2.0 mi west (blackwater, tidally influenced downstream but fresh at this reach); Reaves Ferry Landing is 1.3 mi. Corridor flooding is a live local grievance, not a marketing invention — residents have petitioned Horry County Council over recurring flooding and traffic on SC 90 and asked it to slow rezonings.

facts.turf_specifics: Two distinct soil regimes inside one city. Oceanfront and beach-ridge blocks sit on Newhan-type dune sand: excessively drained, very rapid permeability, no regular water table, and up to 35% shell fragments by volume — drainage is a non-issue, but base compaction over shelly sand and continuous wind-blown sand infill into the turf pile are, plus direct salt-spray exposure on the first few blocks. Inland flats (Market Common, the 33rd Ave N corridor, west of the bypass) are coastal flatwoods soils of the Leon type: very poorly to poorly drained sandy marine sediment with a spodic (Bh) hardpan within 30 inches and a seasonal water table at 6–18 inches for 1–4 months a year. On those lots the base must be cut through or vented past the hardpan or the turf sits on a perched bathtub. Elevation 26 ft. Humid subtropical, 2,800+ hours of sun a year — surface-temperature management and infill choice matter for pet and daycare installs.
