facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH THE HARDPAN. Goretown is the page where the drainage engineering IS the sales argument, and there is a fact here good enough to build the whole page on: Goretown sits at 104 feet — the highest ground of any place in this batch — on 100% Leon fine sand, a poorly drained Spodosol whose seasonal high water table comes within SIX INCHES of the surface, because a cemented spodic horizon perches water under clean white sand. Highest ground, wettest soil. That is counterintuitive, it is verifiable from USDA data, and it explains every failed install and every soggy back yard within five miles. So the page leads: 'The sand in Goretown lies to you' — dig a foot and it looks like the best-draining ground in Horry County; the pan underneath is why your neighbour's turf held water all winter and why ours will not. Then the base spec: locate the spodic layer, excavate through or drain across it, daylight the outlet, don't trust percolation. SECONDARY LEAD: acreage with no HOA and no covenant, two miles from Diamondback at Woodland Valley — a real bermuda-speed practice green beside a working farm for someone who is not going to join a club. WHY IT DIFFERS FROM THE NEIGHBOURS: Loris four miles west is the tobacco town with a downtown, a hospital and a high school; Goretown is the farm crossroads outside it with a fire station named after it and 174 people. Allen is Conway's commuter acreage on Nansemond sand with an 18-inch table; Goretown is farm ground on Leon hardpan with a 6-inch table. Nixons Crossroads has the opposite problem entirely — sand that drains too fast. Four places, four genuinely different soil arguments; Goretown owns the hardpan one.

facts.turf_specifics: THIS IS THE STRONGEST TECHNICAL FINDING IN THE WHOLE BATCH. VERIFIED point soil (USDA NRCS SSURGO, queried 2026-09-07 at 34.0270/-78.8210): map unit 130153, LEON FINE SAND — 100% Leon, POORLY DRAINED, hydrologic group A/D, taxonomic class Sandy siliceous thermic AERIC ALAQUODS. Minimum annual depth to water table: 15 cm — roughly SIX INCHES. Flooding: none; ponding: none. Read that against the elevation: Goretown is the HIGHEST of the four places at 104 ft and simultaneously has by far the SHALLOWEST seasonal water table — six inches, versus eighteen at Allen and Nixonville and sixty at Nixons Crossroads. The reason is that Leon is a Spodosol: an organic-and-aluminium-cemented spodic horizon sits under clean grey sand and perches water on top of it. That is the classic Carolina 'hardpan', and it is exactly the soil that fools installers, because you dig eight inches of loose white sand, conclude it drains beautifully, and then watch the install hold water all winter. Every Goretown job needs the spodic layer located, and the base has to be designed to get water sideways to a daylighted outlet rather than down through a pan that will not take it. Named local drainage: Buck Creek, Sheepbridge Branch, Bear Branch, Mill Branch. Salt exposure: none — 17–18 miles inland. Irrigation is almost certainly private wells (NOT verified).

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH: THIS IS THE ONE THAT ISN'T A BEACH RENTAL. Thomasboro's ZIP is 81% occupied and only 15% seasonal, while every other ZIP in this batch is roughly half empty and 38–42% seasonal. Median age 65.4, median home value $308,600, median build year 2003, 89.6% owner-occupied — the highest owner rate in the batch. So the page is written to a full-time retired homeowner in a 2000s golf-subdivision ranch who is not renting the place out, is not leaving in October, and has simply had enough of mowing, edging, fertilising and irrigating a lawn that stays wet. The technical hook, and it is TRUE ONLY HERE: Thomasboro's soil sample contains no dune sand at all — no Kureb, no Wando, no Newhan — just Goldsboro, Lynchburg, Rains, Pantego, Torhunta, Grifton, a borrow pit and open water. It is the wettest, flattest, most purely Atlantic Coast Flatwoods ground of the four, with a seasonal high water table within six inches of grade on the Rains and Lynchburg soils. So the promise is: a lawn that stays green and firm in a place where the natural lawn stays soggy — and the method is drainage engineering, base depth and a real outlet. Secondary beat unique to this town: it is the closest of the four to the state line, and Farmstead Golf Links' 767-yard par-6 18th literally starts in SC and finishes in NC — the perfect line for saying this crew works both sides of the border and knows the two states' rules differ. WHY THIS DIFFERS FROM ITS NEIGHBOURS: Grissettown 3.3 miles east is the wealthy putting-green page ($463k median, high ground, four Big Cats courses). Seaside is the salt-and-marsh page. Civietown is the schools-and-fields page. Thomasboro is the only one whose defining fact is that people are actually HOME — so it is the everyday residential and pet-turf page, sold on year-round livability and wet ground, and it should carry the small-lot fence rule (4 ft front-yard maximum in R-6000/SBR-6000/MR-3200) because dog runs are the natural upsell to this exact buyer.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: Unincorporated Brunswick County — the County UDO governs, not Calabash's or Carolina Shores' code, though the page should note that ETJ boundaries in this corridor are worth confirming parcel by parcel. Same UDO Impervious Surface definition applies and it is the key regulatory beat: 'compacted earth (such as marl and coquina), gravel, concrete, asphalt' are impervious; 'porous pavement, uncovered wooden slatted decks and the water area of a swimming pool are considered pervious'; artificial turf is unnamed. Brunswick County Stormwater Permit may be required (UDO 3.9.1) — and on soils this wet, stormwater review is a live risk, not a formality. Fence heights (UDO 6.10.1) matter more here than anywhere else in the batch because the lots are small: in R-6000, SBR-6000 and MR-3200 the front-yard maximum is only 4 ft (6 ft in other yards, 8 ft by administrative adjustment), while RR and R-7500 allow 6 ft front and 6 ft elsewhere. HOA GAP: Brunswick Plantation, Crow Creek and Carolina Shores covenants on artificial turf could not be retrieved from public sources; client must pull CC&Rs. NC Planned Community Act (NCGS Ch. 47F) governs these associations generally, but there is no NC statute protecting a homeowner's right to install artificial turf — the association's covenants control, and that is a genuine difference from some western states worth stating plainly.

But the SURROUNDING palette is what separates this town: within a ~1.2 km box, Thomasboro returns Goldsboro, Lynchburg, Rains, Pantego, Torhunta, Grifton, Baymeade — plus map units literally named 'Pits' (a borrow pit) and 'Water'. There is NO Kureb, NO Wando, NO Newhan, NO Pactolus — that is, no excessively drained dune sand anywhere in the sample. Thomasboro is the flattest, loamiest, wettest of the four: essentially pure Atlantic Coast Flatwoods. Lynchburg ('Atlantic Coast Flatwoods' is in the official map unit name), Rains, Pantego and Torhunta are all somewhat poorly to very poorly drained, and SSURGO seasonal high water table for NC019 puts Rains and Lynchburg within about 6 inches of the surface and Pantego and Torhunta at the surface. Salt exposure: low — this is 3.4 mi inland of Calabash and has no ocean frontage. The turf argument here is not salt and it is not slope, it is standing water: base depth, positive fall, and a real outlet or the lawn becomes a bathtub.

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH DRAINAGE AND ACREAGE — the wet-lot fix, not the beach-lifestyle pitch. Hickory Grove is the only one of these four places that is inland, unincorporated, un-HOA'd, and built on perched-water flatwoods soil. The customer here is not choosing turf because a covenant bans a brown lawn or because salt killed the centipede; they are choosing it because a flat, poorly drained acre in Horry County flatwoods turns into a mud sheet from December to April, the dogs track it through the house, the kids can't use the yard, and mowing an acre of bahia in July is a chore they'd like to delete. So the page leads: 'Backyard's been a mud pit since Christmas? On SC 905 flatwoods soil, that's the water table, not your grass.' Then: engineered sub-drainage under the turf, big-dog pet turf runs, and a real backyard putting green — which matters MORE here than on the coast precisely because there is no course across the street, and because there is no HOA and no city permit desk to ask. That freedom-to-build note is the exact inverse of the Cherry Grove page, which leads with a code rule. It is also the inverse of Arcadian Shores, where the enemy is shade, and of Springmaid Beach, which is not a residential page at all. RESEARCH FLAG: this is the thinnest of the four places by a wide margin. It supports one honest, drainage-led page. If the client wants volume here, the right move is to fold Hickory Grove into a broader 'SC 905 corridor / Conway-to-Longs' page rather than manufacture depth that the community does not have.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: NONE FOUND, AND THAT IS THE STORY. Hickory Grove is unincorporated: no municipal zoning administrator, no city impervious-surface cap, no architectural review board, no HOA covenants. It sits entirely outside North Myrtle Beach's Chapter 23 impervious limits and outside the City of Myrtle Beach's code. What does apply is Horry County zoning and the county's stormwater/land-disturbance rules — and I could not verify their residential thresholds: horrycountysc.gov refused the connection during this session and the county code on Municode returned 403. FLAG FOR FOLLOW-UP: confirm (a) whether Horry County requires a land-disturbance permit below the 1-acre NPDES threshold, and (b) whether any county landscape/impervious standard touches residential turf. Until then the page should say 'no city permit process out here — county rules only' and stop, rather than assert a specific exemption. Also note SC LLR licensing applies statewide (residential work above the state's dollar threshold requires the appropriate SC license) — relevant because this is the SC side of the client's cross-state polygon, not Brunswick County NC.
facts.turf_specifics: The defining condition is INLAND FLATWOODS DRAINAGE, not salt. Hickory Grove sits ~10 miles inland on the outer Coastal Plain; there is no salt spray, no beach-ridge sand, no tidal influence. Instead the soils are the poorly to somewhat-poorly drained loamy sands typical of inland Horry County — the Rains, Lynchburg, Goldsboro, Foreston and Norfolk series associations — where a seasonal high water table perches within roughly 0.5 to 1.5 feet of the surface through winter and spring, and where flat topography gives water nowhere to go. The near-surface argillic (clay-increase) horizon is what causes the perched water, and it is also what will defeat a turf install that assumes free-draining sand. PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE FOR THE INSTALLER: a coastal-style install (permeable backing over 3-4 inches of #57 stone, drain to daylight) does not work if there is no daylight and the receiving soil accepts 0.5 in/hr. Hickory Grove jobs need a designed subsurface — French drain or perforated pipe under the aggregate, positive fall to a swale or ditch, and in the worst lots a shallow dry well or connection to the roadside ditch network. Irrigation restriction is a non-issue (private wells). Grub, mole cricket and fire-ant pressure in native centipede/bahia lawns is a legitimate secondary argument. CAVEAT: soil series above are the standard inland-Horry association, stated from general Coastal Plain soils knowledge, not from a parcel-level USDA Web Soil Survey pull in this session — run WSS on a real address before printing a series name on the page.

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH RENTAL TURNOVER, NOT CURB APPEAL. Eighty percent of Holden Beach houses are second homes and rentals whose owner is 200 miles away; they absorb roughly 16,800 people at peak and 12,600 on an ordinary summer week, and then sit empty from Labor Day to Memorial Day with nobody to mow, water or reseed. The page's argument is a ground plane that survives twenty renters a season, salt spray from two directions, blown sand, and six months of no maintenance visits — under-house parking areas and dune walkovers where grass has literally never grown in Newhan sand. Then hang the technical credibility on the one thing no competitor's page mentions: Holden Beach wrote its own stormwater ordinance in 1998 specifically because it wanted to be stricter than the state, it requires you to keep the water on your own lot, and it regulates the fill you place — so the base build is a permitting question, not a preference. That is a completely different page from Ocean Isle Beach next door. OIB is a 67.9-median-age retirement town with four championship golf courses at its own mailing address and $100k household incomes — that page leads with backyard putting greens for people with time and money. Holden Beach has no golf, no HOA, and no year-round residents to speak of; its page leads with durability, absentee ownership, and the town's unusually aggressive on-lot stormwater rule.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: The strongest and most checkable regulatory hook in this batch. Holden Beach has had its OWN stormwater management ordinance since 1998, and the town's plan states its purpose plainly: 'to provide greater protection than offered through state regulations and to retain stormwater on individual lots to ensure residential development does not adversely impact adjacent properties.' It also explicitly regulates 'placement of fill materials on the island' — which is exactly what a turf base is. New development 'is required to install a stormwater system by using swales or catch basins that flow into a subsurface system' (LUP Ch.4). Policy 3.1.J commits the town to requiring all new commercial and residential development to treat stormwater onsite with BMPs; Policy 3.1.E endorses Low Impact Development in the Lockwood Folly watershed including 'maximizing the use of permeable pavements, reducing the amount of impervious coverage.' Permits confirmed by the town: new construction, demolition, pool, sand fence exemption, CAMA minor, delineation. 'All work in the water, over the water or within 75 feet of the water requires written authorization.' CAMA's 75' Estuarine AEC is described in the plan as serving 'to limit impervious surfaces adjacent to sensitive natural areas.' GAP: I could NOT read the actual Holden Beach code (Chapter 157 zoning) — it is hosted on codelibrary.amlegal.com behind a Cloudflare bot check I did not bypass — so I have no verified numeric lot-coverage or built-upon-area percentage for the town. Client must call HB Planning & Inspections, 910-842-6080, and ask two questions: (1) does the town count synthetic turf as built-upon area, and (2) does a turf base count as regulated 'fill' under the 1998 stormwater ordinance.
facts.turf_specifics: Two soils, and they behave oppositely. The developed ridge is Newhan Fine Sand — 'gently sloping, excessively drained sands located throughout the island in upland areas and built-upon lots' (HB LUP Ch.3). Water drops straight through; the failure mode is base migration and settlement, not ponding. The undeveloped and marsh-edge land is Carteret loamy sand — 'very poorly drained sandy soils often found in tidal marshes… saturated continuously with water and flooded twice daily by tides.' Around the dredged finger canals the fill is literally dredge spoil, placed when the canals were cut to create the island's current configuration. Majority of the island sits in the 100-year floodplain (AE and AO zones). Salt exposure is total — ocean on one side, ICWW and canal water on the other, houses elevated on pilings so the whole ground plane is under-house shade and blown sand. Island is on central sewer (West Brunswick Regional WWTP), so no septic drainfield constraint — unlike Ash and Longwood.
facts.housing_stock: An 8-mile barrier island of almost nothing but detached rental cottages on pilings. 2020 Census: 2,335 total housing units, 296 occupied, 2,039 vacant. The town's own CAMA Land Use Plan (certified 5 May 2021) puts it at 2,491 units in 2016, of which 2,257 (91%) were single-family; only 494 occupied year-round (~20%), 1,588 seasonal/recreational, 409 other vacant — 80.2% vacant/seasonal. The building era is unusually tight: 715 units built 1980-89 and 709 built 1990-99, i.e. 1,424 of ~2,500 units (57%) went up in two decades, then 447 in 2000-09 and 214 in 2010-16. Lots are small platted beach lots — vacant land averages roughly 0.23 acre/parcel (884 vacant parcels over 231 acres) and buildout math assumes ~865 more units on 167 acres of R-1. Zoning is R-1 and R-2 residential, C-1 commercial, plus C (Conservation), R (Rural) and RS (Rural Special Use). No master HOA governs the island — this is individually owned fee-simple beach lots, not a plantation community, which is the structural difference from Ocean Isle Beach's mainland side. Median household income is the highest of any jurisdiction charted in the 2025 Ocean Isle Beach plan, above OIB's own ~$100k.
facts.who_lives_there: Almost nobody, most of the year. Permanent population 921 (2020 Census); 633 per the state demographer in 2016. Median age 62.1, 39.3% aged 65+. The town's plan estimates peak seasonal overnight population at 16,797 — 28 times the permanent population — plus ~1,356 day-trippers a day computed from 226 public parking spaces. Even a normal summer weekday runs ~12,600. Owner survey during the plan update: 70% of respondents were second-home owners; the rest were seasonal visitors, off-island residents and year-round renters. So the buyer is an absentee owner in Charlotte, Greensboro or Raleigh (the island's street grid is literally named for those cities) who visits a few weeks a year and rents the house the rest of the season.
facts.golf: No golf course on the island. Nearest named courses: Lockwood Folly Country Club, 19 Clubhouse Drive, Supply NC 28462 — same ZIP as Holden Beach, directly across the Lockwood Folly River/Inlet that forms the island's east boundary. Carolina National Golf Club, 1643 Goley Hewett Road SE, Bolivia NC 28422. Both confirmed in the Brunswick County TDA course directory. Golf is NOT the Holden Beach angle — this is the one town in the batch where a putting-green lead would be wrong.
facts.commercial_targets: Thin on the island itself — commercial is only 29 parcels and 12.67 acres, 0.57% of the planning jurisdiction, and there is no school on the island. Real targets: (1) the Town of Holden Beach itself — Bridgeview Park's playground and splashpad surrounds, the Pavilion's event lawn, and the causeway, which residents ranked 'Improve Causeway Appearance' as their #3 desire (11 votes) in the plan's public input. (2) A DOG PARK. Residents ranked it #6 among desires (5 votes) at the public input meeting and the town still has none — a shovel-ready pitch to the Parks & Rec Board. (3) The vacation-rental management companies, which are the real decision-makers for 1,588 seasonal units — one management contract is worth more than fifty homeowner calls. (4) Off-island but same ZIP: Lockwood Folly Country Club (Supply). Note there is NO school, daycare or pet business enumerated inside town limits.
facts.landmarks: Holden Beach Bridge — the high-rise steel and concrete span dedicated 13 May 1986, the only way on. Holden Beach Pavilion, built 2007 next to the boating access facility, with a paved dancefloor, covered picnic shelters, Wi-Fi and an ICWW fishing/observation pier; it hosts the town's festivals and summer concerts. Bridgeview Park on Davis Street — basketball/pickleball court, bocce courts, playground, picnic area, splashpad, showers, transient dock and kayak launch. Halstead Street Park (0.14 acre, north end of Halstead St). Sand Dollar Park (5.83 acres at the end of Sand Dollar Drive, mostly marsh). The Holden Beach Fitness Trail/PAR Course — nine exercise stations along the Ocean Blvd West sidewalk between Greensboro Street and Scotch Bonnet Drive, built 2012. Town Hall, 110 Rothschild Street. Tri-Beach Volunteer Fire Department. Lockwood Folly Inlet (east) and Shallotte Inlet (west). Street names locals use as landmarks: Ocean Boulevard East/West, Brunswick Avenue East, Scotch Bonnet Drive, Marker Fifty Five.

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH THE 55+ PATIO LOT AND THE MUNICIPAL BALL FIELD — two things no other town in this batch has together. Little River's median age is 60.1 and 39.3% of residents are 65 or older; 29.5% of its housing sits vacant most of the year. It is, demographically, a retirement town wearing a fishing village's clothes, and it is the only one of these four where the customer's actual sentence is 'I don't want to mow it any more, and I'm gone from May to October.' So the residential lead is low-maintenance turf on small golf-community and 55+ patio lots (5,000–8,000 sq ft), specced so a snowbird's yard looks identical in March as it did in November — plus backyard putting greens sold into the densest golf cluster in the service area, with Glen Dornoch, River Hills, Eagle Nest, Heather Glen, Long Bay and Eastport all inside the CDP and Tidewater, Barefoot, The Pearl, Oyster Bay and Sea Trail minutes away. That is a completely different lead from Socastee's drainage story and Red Hill's ARC-approval story. The second lead, and the one the owner cares about most, is that the North Myrtle Beach Park & Sports Complex — 160 acres, 25 fields — is INSIDE the Little River CDP. This should be the page that carries the municipal sports-field case. And the technical differentiator to work in everywhere: salt. Little River's inlet and waterway exposure means fastener metallurgy and backing spec actually matter here in a way they do not fifteen miles inland — that is the credibility detail that separates a real installer from a franchise page.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: (1) Horry County Stormwater Ordinance: 0.5-acre disturbance triggers a permit; single-family residential exempt. (2) Unincorporated — no town architectural review. The real constraint is the golf-community and age-restricted covenant, and Little River's 55+ and golf communities carry the most restrictive landscape standards in the batch. Under the SC Homeowners Association Act (Title 27, Ch. 30), those covenants and any rules must be recorded with the Horry County Register of Deeds — annually by 10 January for rules — or they are not enforceable. (3) Waterfront and marsh-front work near the tidal critical line falls under the SC Coastal Tidelands and Wetlands Act / OCRM jurisdiction, now administered by the SC Department of Environmental Services (SCDES) following DHEC's 2024 split. Verify the critical-area line before regrading a waterway-front back yard. (4) HONEST NEGATIVE FINDING: no SC statute found protecting a homeowner's right to install turf against HOA objection.
facts.turf_specifics: Tidal, brackish and salt-loaded — the spec genuinely differs from inland Horry County. Little River sits where the Atlantic Intracoastal Waterway meets Little River Inlet at the North Carolina state line; the CDP is marsh, swamp, tidal creek and scrub-pine flatwoods bounded by the Waccamaw River and the AIWW. Salt aerosol off the inlet and waterway, brackish groundwater, and marsh-edge lots with a water table near the surface at high tide argue for stainless or polymer fasteners rather than plain galvanised nails, salt- and UV-stable backing, and infill that will not crust. Soils are the same Atlantic Coast Flatwoods sands as the rest of the county — Leon-type profiles, very poorly to poorly drained, spodic hardpan within 30 in (typically 15–22 in), seasonal high water table commonly 6–18 in. Marsh-adjacent lots also sit near the state's tidal critical-area line, which brings OCRM jurisdiction into play before any grading.
facts.housing_stock: 8,351 housing units: 4,511 owner-occupied (54.0%), 1,375 renter-occupied (16.5%), and 2,465 VACANT (29.5%) — a seasonal/second-home share roughly triple Socastee's and Red Hill's. Median home value $305,800 (hometownlocator, 2020–2024 ACS); city-data puts the 2024 median house/condo value at $345,766. Median household income $65,786; per capita $41,786. 10.82 sq mi, 1,126 people/sq mi. Population 7,027 (2000) → 8,960 (2010) → 11,711 (2020) — 67% growth in twenty years, so the stock skews heavily post-1995. The market is a barbell: (a) waterfront cottages and condos in the old village near the shrimp docks; (b) a very large volume of golf-community and active-adult/55+ patio homes along US 17, SC 9, SC 57 and SC 90 — Eagle Nest, Glen Dornoch, River Hills, Heather Glen, Long Bay, the Harbourgate/Lightkeepers area near the inlet, plus Barefoot Resort straddling toward North Myrtle Beach; (c) manufactured-home and RV communities inland. HOA-HEAVY in the golf and 55+ communities, and those covenants are the tightest in the service area. Typical lots in the patio-home and zero-lot-line products run roughly 5,000–8,000 sq ft — exactly the size where a full-yard turf conversion pencils. GAP: a median-year-built figure specific to the Little River CDP could not be sourced this session (see notes).
facts.who_lives_there: Retirees, decisively. MEDIAN AGE 60.1 and 39.3% of residents aged 65 or older — by far the oldest of the four and one of the oldest CDPs on the Grand Strand. 84% white, 5.7% Black, 4.3% Hispanic. Add snowbirds who are gone half the year, boaters and charter-fishing people, a growing remote-worker slice, and inland working families. Historically Little River grew as the low-tax, no-municipal-government alternative to North Myrtle Beach, and during South Carolina's 21-year video-poker era it was nicknamed 'Little Reno' for its North Carolina border trade.
facts.golf: The densest golf cluster in the whole service area. IN Little River: Eagle Nest Golf Club, 3820 Fairway Drive; Glen Dornoch Waterway Golf Links, 4840 Glen Dornoch Way (Clyde Johnston, opened 1996, 260 acres, finishing holes along the Intracoastal); River Hills Golf & Country Club, 3670 Cedar Creek Run (Tom Jackson, ~40-ft elevation changes, Golfweek Top 50 Southeast); The Valley at Eastport Golf Club, 4355 Eastport Blvd; Heather Glen Golf Links (27 holes, named best new public course in America on opening in 1987); Long Bay Club. IMMEDIATELY ADJACENT: Tidewater Golf Club, Beachwood Golf Club (1520 US-17 S) and Surf Golf & Beach Club (1701 Springland Lane), North Myrtle Beach; Barefoot Resort's four championship courses. OVER THE NC LINE, minutes away: The Pearl Golf Club (1300 Pearl Blvd) and Brunswick Plantation (380 Brunswick Drive) and Crow Creek (490 S Crow Creek Drive), Calabash; Thistle Golf Club (1815 Olde Thistle Club Rd), Oyster Bay Golf Links (614 Lakeshore Drive) and Sea Trail Golf Links (75 Clubhouse Road), Sunset Beach.
facts.commercial_targets: THE SINGLE BEST COMMERCIAL TARGET IN THIS BATCH: North Myrtle Beach Park & Sports Complex, 150 Citizens Circle, Little River, SC 29566 — a 160-acre municipal complex with 12 baseball/softball fields (4 youth baseball / collegiate softball, 4 high school / collegiate baseball), 13 soccer/lacrosse fields (8 of them regulation), 16 batting cages, an amphitheatre, 3 miles of trails, 5 playgrounds and 11 picnic shelters, hosting year-round tournaments. It is owned and operated by the City of North Myrtle Beach but sits physically inside unincorporated Little River — which is precisely the municipal ball-field work the owner says he wants. Phone (843) 281-3800. Also: North Strand Recreation Center and North Strand Park, 120 Hwy 57 South, Little River (Horry County Parks & Recreation). Schools: North Myrtle Beach High School, 3750 Sea Mountain Highway, Little River 29566 (football, baseball, softball, soccer); North Myrtle Beach Middle School on SC-90, Little River; Riverside Elementary School, Hwy 57 N, Little River; Waterway Elementary. Pet: Saint Francis Animal Hospital, 1384 US-17, Little River; Banfield Pet Hospital, 1370 US-17 N; PetSmart, 1530 US-17 N; Petco, 596 US-17 N; The Pet Stop; Jen's Ocean Drive Pet Grooming, 301 Main St, NMB. Childcare: Shoot for the Moon Academy #6, 1699 US Highway 17, Little River — the ONLY named licensed centre that surfaced inside the CDP; treat childcare as a research gap here.
facts.landmarks: The Little River waterfront on Mineola Avenue — a working shrimping fleet, commercial fishing operations, deep-sea charter boats and dinner cruises. The Big M Casino, South Carolina's only casino boat, sailing two yachts into federal waters. Vereen Memorial Historical Gardens (roughly 14 miles of trails through maritime forest, tidal creeks and coastal wetlands). The World Famous Blue Crab Festival every May and the Shrimp Festival in October. Twelve 33 Distillery. Grande Harbour Marina; Coquina Harbour; Cricket Cove Marina; the Dry Dock Marina at NMB RV Resort. The Little River Inlet jetties. Captain Smiley and Fine Catch fishing charters. SC 31 (Carolina Bays Parkway) northern terminus. Seaside Furniture Gallery.

name: Ocean Isle Beach

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH THE BACKYARD PUTTING GREEN AND THE ARC SUBMITTAL. Ocean Isle Beach is the only town in this batch where the golf lead is factually earned rather than borrowed: four championship courses carry an Ocean Isle Beach mailing address, the median age is 67.9, median household income is just under $100,000, and seventy percent of adults are out of the labor force. That is a customer with a golf habit, discretionary money, and every weekday free — living in mainland plantation subdivisions where an architectural review committee has to approve the job. So the page sells two things at once: a practice green with a stated, verifiable ball-roll speed, and a submittal package the ARC will actually approve — drawings, drainage detail, material spec. Second-order angle for the same page: the town's own residents told their planners they want impervious surfaces reduced and green space required, so position turf as the drainage-positive alternative to a paver patio, not as a lawn substitute. Contrast with Holden Beach seven miles east, which has no golf course, no HOA, no architectural review and only 921 permanent residents — that page is about rental durability. Contrast with Ash inland, where the median income is $54k and 44% of homes are manufactured — a putting-green page there would be aimed at nobody.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: The Town's Code of Ordinances covers Zoning (R-1, C-1/C-2/C-3, mixed-use, with lot size, height and setback standards plus site lighting and 'appearance standards' governing the external presentation of properties, particularly in commercial zones), Subdivision (drainage systems, lot configuration, street design), and Flood Damage Prevention with a designated Floodplain Administrator. Public input during the 2025 plan update produced a directly usable quote: residents 'opposed new neighborhoods… due to concerns about preserving natural beauty and reducing impervious surfaces that contribute to additional stormwater runoff and flood risks,' and recommended 'requiring green space in new developments.' Policy 2.1.H restricts land uses and building heights around the airport. GAP: I could NOT read the actual OIB code — oibgov.com returns HTTP 403 to every automated request, browser included — so there is no verified numeric impervious-surface or lot-coverage limit here. Client must call OIB Building Inspections and ask whether synthetic turf counts toward lot coverage, and separately must confirm the Ocean Ridge Plantation and Brick Landing POA architectural-review requirements for turf, which are the real gatekeepers on the mainland side.
facts.turf_specifics: The plan is blunt: 'Most soils in Ocean Isle Beach are not suitable for development' and most have 'somewhat limited or very limited development suitability.' Drainage is bipolar — 'most soils along the shoreline are excessively drained while soils on the mainland and within the ETJ range from very poorly drained to excessively drained.' All soils in town and ETJ have very limited septic absorption capacity, but the town is on central sewer so that constrains site work rather than turf. Nearly 800 acres of non-coastal (freshwater, wooded) wetlands. The island is a 5-mile barrier strip from Tubbs Inlet to Shallotte Inlet with dredged finger canals through the older neighborhoods; the plan warns that 'long-standing neighborhoods along the canals' face permanent inundation from sea level rise within the lifespan of a single-family home. Residents specifically flagged 'inadequate drainage systems, especially along Moore Street where repeated home flooding was reported.' Salt exposure from ocean, ICWW and canals. Irrigation note worth using: Brunswick County runs 25+ miles of reuse force mains delivering treated wastewater to eleven golf courses and 1,040 acres of dedicated tree farms and turf farms — the sod farms are a named local competitor for the natural-grass alternative.
facts.housing_stock: 3,290 housing units today, 2,285 of them single-family detached, per the Town's CAMA & Comprehensive Plan certified 3 October 2025. About 87% of the stock is vacant per ACS, and 2,030 units are specifically 'seasonal, recreational, or occasional use.' The Town has just approved a subdivision of roughly 650 single-family homes — a ~20% increase in the entire housing stock in one approval, on the east end. ZIP 28469 (island + mainland/ETJ) shows 9,258 units, median year built 2001, median home value $463,200 — the newest and by far the most valuable stock in this batch. Zoning is R-1 residential plus C-1/C-2/C-3 commercial and mixed-use, with lot size, height and setback standards; the Town has enforced subdivision regulations since 1975. Existing land use inside the jurisdiction: 1,023 acres residential across 5,097 parcels, 1,232 acres still vacant, 403 acres of approved-but-unbuilt 'Pending Development', 96 acres commercial, 72 acres airport, 62 acres recreational. The mainland side is where the HOA-governed plantation subdivisions sit (Ocean Ridge Plantation, Brick Landing Plantation) — architectural review is the norm there and absent on the island.
facts.who_lives_there: Retirees with money. 867 permanent residents (2020 Census), median age 67.9 (ACS 2023), and the plan states flatly that Ocean Isle Beach 'is predominantly a retirement community with almost 70% of the population aged 16 years and older not in the labor force.' Median household income just under $100,000 — roughly $30,000 above the North Carolina median and higher than every nearby jurisdiction except Holden Beach. 98% White. Growth since 2000 has been 'driven primarily by in-migration of retirees and second-home owners rather than by natural increase.' Arts, entertainment and recreation plus accommodation and food services account for ~72% of employment. Compared with Ash (median age 46.3, income $54k, working households) this is a completely different customer.
facts.golf: This is the golf town of the four, and the courses carry an Ocean Isle Beach address. The four 'Big Cats' courses of Ocean Ridge Plantation, operated by Ocean Ridge Golf, Inc. at 351 Ocean Ridge Parkway SW, Ocean Isle Beach NC 28469: Tiger's Eye, Leopard's Chase (6330 Castlebrook Way, Ocean Isle Beach NC 28469), Panther's Run and Lion's Paw Golf Links — all four confirmed on bigcatsgolf.com and in the county TDA directory. Brick Landing Plantation Golf Club, Ocean Isle Beach (named in Sea Trail's regional course list; street address not verified). Immediately adjacent: Sea Trail Golf Resort, 75A Clubhouse Road, Sunset Beach NC 28468; Oyster Bay Golf Links, 614 Lakeshore Drive, Sunset Beach NC 28468; The Pearl Golf Links, Calabash NC 28467; Crow Creek, 490 S Crow Creek Drive, Calabash NC 28467; Meadowlands Golf Club, 1000 Meadowlands Trail, Calabash NC 28467; Brunswick Plantation Resort and Golf, 380 Brunswick Drive NW, Calabash NC 28467.
facts.commercial_targets: (1) Ocean Ridge Plantation / Ocean Ridge Golf, Inc., 351 Ocean Ridge Parkway SW — four championship courses under one operator is the single highest-value commercial call in this batch: practice greens, teeing-ground surrounds, cart-path shoulders, clubhouse landscape. (2) Brick Landing Plantation Golf Club, on the ICWW. (3) Odell Williamson Municipal Airport — 72 acres of town-adjacent institutional ground. (4) The Town of Ocean Isle Beach itself: 62 acres of recreational land across 4 parcels, plus the plan's stated goal of 'expanding parks, events, and recreation' and the resident demand for a senior/community center. (5) The developer of the 650-home east-end subdivision — model-home landscapes and amenity areas, decided once, at the top. (6) Museum of Coastal Carolina (outdoor/entry landscape). (7) The plantation POA architectural review committees on the mainland, which approve or kill every residential turf job in Ocean Ridge and Brick Landing.
facts.landmarks: The Odell Williamson Bridge on NC 904 — the ONLY vehicular access to the island, pre-stressed concrete, chronically congested in season, and named in the plan as the town's top infrastructure vulnerability. Odell Williamson Municipal Airport, 72 acres, the largest single non-residential parcel in town. Museum of Coastal Carolina (dioramas, touch tanks, Civil War and Native American artifacts). The roundabout with its three bronze statues of children flying kites. Ocean Isle Fishing Pier (damaged by Hurricane Isaias, 2020). Town Hall, which houses the Emergency Command Center. The dredged canal neighborhoods. Tubbs Inlet (west) and Shallotte Inlet (east). Public beach accesses every 500 feet. The east end, where the ~650-home subdivision is going in. Residents have asked repeatedly for a senior or community center the town does not yet have.

name: Allen

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH: the private backyard practice complex on land you actually own, with nobody to ask. Allen is the only one of these four places where (a) the nearest golf course is roughly nine miles away, (b) lots are measured in acres rather than feet, and (c) most parcels sit outside any HOA and outside Horry County's stormwater permit trigger because single-family residential is exempt. That combination is a putting-green page, not a lawn-replacement page: a two- or three-hole short-game area, a chipping surface, a bunker, built on ground where nobody reviews the plans. The technical hook that makes it credible: Nansemond loamy fine sand with an 18-inch seasonal water table and scattered Woodington/Rutlege wet pockets, so the green has to be surveyed and based lot by lot — the same acre that drains like beach sand in September perches water in March. WHY IT DIFFERS FROM THE NEIGHBOURS: Conway five miles south is inside city limits with city permitting; Nixonville is quarter-acre HOA new-build where a green won't fit; Loris is a tobacco town with a downtown; Goretown is farm ground on hardpan. Allen is specifically Conway's unzoned-feeling north acreage fringe — working families with room, not retirees with covenants.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: VERIFIED: Horry County Stormwater Management and Sediment Control Ordinance took effect Oct 1, 2000 and was re-enacted July 2017; a stormwater permit is required for land disturbance of 0.5 acre or more, and single-family residential construction, agricultural land uses, timbering and minor residential subdivisions are EXEMPT. For a typical residential turf install in Allen that means no county stormwater permit — say so plainly on the page, it removes a buyer objection. VERIFIED (pending): a proposed county landscape ordinance requiring a 15-foot buffer from all wetlands had first reading scheduled 21 April 2026 (deferred from 17 March 2026); Horry County's existing code offers a voluntary 50-foot wetland buffer under its sustainable-development option for multi-residential projects, which developers routinely decline. HONEST GAP: horrycountysc.gov was unreachable from this session on 2026-09-07 (connection refused on both WebFetch and curl), so I could not open the county zoning ordinance or fence regulations directly; and a Municode API search of Horry County (client 6287) for 'artificial turf', 'synthetic turf', 'impervious' and 'fence' returned zero hits for ALL FOUR terms including 'fence', which means the search endpoint was non-functional rather than that the terms are absent. Do not publish a claim that Horry County has no artificial-turf rule until someone re-checks. HOA: no county-wide HOA prevalence data found; the named subdivisions above will have builder HOAs, the acreage will not.
facts.turf_specifics: VERIFIED point soil (USDA NRCS SSURGO, queried 2026-09-07 at 33.9208/-79.0403): map unit 130158, Nansemond loamy fine sand, 0 to 2 percent slopes — 95% Nansemond, moderately well drained, hydrologic group A/D, taxonomic class Coarse-loamy siliceous subactive thermic Aquic Hapludults. Minor components: Woodington 2% (poorly drained) and Rutlege 2% (very poorly drained). Minimum annual depth to water table: 46 cm (~18 inches). Flooding frequency: None. Ponding: none. Elevation 63 ft. What that means on a job: the surface drains like sand but the A/D dual hydrologic group means once the seasonal water table comes up to 18 inches the same soil behaves like group D — the base perches. The Woodington/Rutlege inclusions mean a single one-acre lot can contain a genuinely wet pocket next to genuinely dry ground; you cannot spec one base depth for the whole yard from a windshield look. Surrounding named drainage features (OSM): Maple Swamp, Poplar Swamp, Boggy Swamp, Brown Swamp, Grier Swamp, Long Swamp, Mill Branch, Cross Branch, Smith Branch, Booth Branch. Salt exposure: effectively none — roughly 18 miles inland, no tidal water within the corridor. Irrigation: likely private wells on the acreage lots (NOT verified this session) — worth confirming, because well-water iron staining on light infill is a real objection and a real selling point for turf.
facts.housing_stock: THIN — no census place, no CDP, no tract-level data exists for Allen itself. Verified: OSM hamlet node at 33.9208, -79.0403; elevation 63 ft (USGS 3DEP); post office operated 1907–1927 only; ~5 mi north of Conway; sits 0.4 mi off US 701, 1.5 mi from SC 22 (Veterans Highway / Conway Bypass) and 1.8 mi from SC 319 (Adrian Highway). INFERRED (not measured — flag this to the client): rural Conway-fringe stock — older farmhouses, 1970s–90s brick ranches and manufactured homes on half-acre to multi-acre parcels, with a handful of small newer subdivisions dropped in: Wisteria Woods (0.4 mi), Westwood Reserves (2.8 mi), Kingston Oaks (2.9 mi), Ivy Glen (3.6 mi). Outside those pockets this is non-HOA land — the acreage lots have no architectural review, no covenant on ground cover, no POA. That is the single most commercially useful fact about Allen and it is the opposite of Nixons Crossroads.
facts.who_lives_there: THIN — no census data. INFERRED from geography: this is Conway's north commuter fringe, not a retirement or tourist zone. SC 22 puts the beach ~25 min away and US 701 puts downtown Conway 5 min away, so the plausible profile is year-round working households, multi-generational rural families, and Conway/CCU-adjacent employment — not seasonal owners. There is no beach rental economy here and no golf-community retiree cluster. Do NOT write this page in retiree voice.
facts.golf: Allen is the ONLY one of the four with no course within walking or short-drive distance. Nearest OSM-verified courses: Wild Wing Golf Course (Wild Wing Blvd, Conway) 9.2 mi; General James Hackler Course at Coastal Carolina University (Citadel Drive, Conway) 9.5 mi; King's North at Myrtle Beach National 9.5 mi. CAVEAT: OpenStreetMap's Horry County golf layer is incomplete — it is missing Shaftesbury Glen Golf & Fish Club (Conway), Burning Ridge (Conway) and The Witch (Conway), all confirmed by GolfPass's Conway directory but not coordinate-verified in this session. Even allowing for those, the nearest tee is a drive, not a walk.
facts.commercial_targets: Coastal Carolina University, Conway (~9.5 mi) — the real anchor: Brooks Stadium, baseball and softball programmes, and the Hackler golf course. This is the closest genuine sports-field target to Allen and it belongs on this page rather than a Myrtle Beach municipal-softball pitch that reads as out-of-area. Academy for Technology & Academics (2.0 mi) — a career/tech campus is a credible indoor-training-surface prospect. Homewood Elementary School (3.4 mi). Conway Christian School (4.3 mi). Conway Education Center, Conway Elementary, SOAR Academy and Horry County Education Center all within 4.5–5 mi. Collins Park, Conway (5.0 mi). Shoreline Behavioral Health Services (1.6 mi). HONEST GAP: no daycare, pet daycare, veterinary practice or kennel was found in OSM within 8 km of Allen — the pet-turf commercial angle is weak here and should not be forced; put pet turf on this page as a residential product (dog runs on acreage), not a commercial one.
facts.landmarks: Horry County Fire / Rescue Station 27 'Allens' (2.8 mi) — the station carries the community's name, which is the single most checkable proof-of-locality on the page. Academy for Technology & Academics, the Horry County Schools career/tech high school (2.0 mi). Shoreline Behavioral Health Services (1.6 mi). Harris Shortcut Road, Long Avenue Extension / SC 65, Bakers Chapel Road, Four Mile Road, Collins-Jollie Road, Adrian Highway (SC 319). Horry County Fire / Rescue Station 21 'Maple' (3.0 mi). Homewood Elementary School (3.4 mi). Neighbouring hamlets a local would name: Adrian, Homewood, Maple Crossroads, Poplar Forks, Saint Paul Forks, Booth. Churches: Homewood Church, Pisgah Church, Poplar Hill Church, Saint Pauls Church, Zion Church, Mount Aeral Church, Maple Baptist Church, Friendship Church, Happy Home Church. CAUTION: 'Poplar School', 'Saint Paul School' and 'Allens School' appear in OSM/GNIS but these are almost certainly historic one-room-school points, not operating schools — do not list them as businesses.

name: Ash

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH THE HALF-ACRE DOG YARD AND THE SEPTIC FIELD — a mud problem, not a golf problem. Ash is 2,658 year-round people at a $53,935 median household income, 79% owner-occupied, 44% of the housing manufactured, median home value $198,100. Nobody here is buying a five-figure putting green, and a page that opens with one is talking past the whole town. What an Ash household actually buys is a pet turf area and a mud-free dog run, a kids' play surface, and a defined patch of yard that stops being a swamp every winter — quoted as a job, not by the acre. Then earn the technical trust with the two things that are uniquely true of unincorporated Brunswick County and true nowhere on the beach: (1) your septic drainfield and its repair area govern where turf can legally and safely go, because the county's RR district is built around individual wells and septic; and (2) the county's own ordinance calls gravel and compacted earth impervious while saying nothing about synthetic turf — so the base is the permit question, and here is how we build and document it. That page cannot be templated from Holden Beach (barrier island, central sewer, 80% absentee rental owners, town stormwater ordinance) or from Ocean Isle Beach (median age 67.9, $100k incomes, four golf courses, HOA architectural review). Ash's differentiator is that it is the only one of the four with real working families, real schools, and real septic fields.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: Because Ash is unincorporated, it falls entirely under the Brunswick County Unified Development Ordinance (edition dated 1/28/2025) administered by the county Planning & Community Enforcement Department, 910-253-2025, which serves 'unincorporated areas of Brunswick County that fall outside the planning jurisdictions of municipalities.' Permits run through bcpp.brunswickcountync.gov. The verbatim UDO Impervious Surface definition (quoted above) is the live regulatory question for turf: gravel and compacted earth are impervious, porous pavement is pervious, turf is unnamed — so how the base is built and documented determines the answer. Also relevant: the county is running a 'UDO Modernization Project,' so this definition is in play. The county's WQP Water Quality Protection Overlay — 25% maximum built-upon impervious area, 30 ft buffer from any wetland or water line, structures at least 75 ft from mean high water, applying to parcels of one acre or more within 575 ft of mean high water — covers the Lockwood Folly River mouth area, not Ash; do not misapply it. No HOA architectural review to clear.
facts.turf_specifics: Ash sits at 49 ft elevation — the highest ground of the four places here and well out of the barrier-island regime. No salt spray, no tidal water table, no CAMA Areas of Environmental Concern. The governing constraint is completely different: individual septic systems. The Brunswick County UDO's RR district expressly anticipates wells and septic tanks, which means on a typical Ash lot the drainfield and its repair area occupy a large share of the buildable yard and cannot be covered with an impermeable system. That is the single most important site question on an Ash job and no competitor's town page mentions it. Second constraint: the county's UDO defines Impervious Surface as 'Any surface which in whole or in part, restricts or prevents the natural absorption of water into the ground. Such surfaces may include, but not be limited to compacted earth (such as marl and coquina), gravel, concrete, asphalt, or other paving material… Porous pavement, uncovered wooden slatted decks and the water area of a swimming pool are considered pervious.' Synthetic turf is named nowhere — but a compacted aggregate base plainly is. Soils in the coastal-plain interior here are generally poorly drained sandy loams over a seasonal high water table; expect standing water and mud in winter rather than the free-draining sand of Holden Beach.
facts.housing_stock: Rural, year-round, and nearly half manufactured. ZIP 28420 (ACS 2023 5-year): 1,513 housing units — 813 single-family detached and 665 mobile homes (44% of all units), with essentially no attached or multifamily stock. 1,163 occupied, 917 owner-occupied (79%), 246 renter. Only 350 vacant and only 125 of those seasonal — 8% seasonal, versus 80%+ on the two beaches. Median year structure built 1989. Median home value $198,100 — less than half the $463,200 in Ocean Isle Beach's ZIP. Because Ash is unincorporated, Brunswick County's Unified Development Ordinance governs, and the applicable district is RR Rural Low Density Residential: minimum lot area 20,000 sq ft (0.46 acre) without public water and sewer, 15,000 sq ft with; 75 ft minimum lot width; 25 ft front and rear yards. The UDO's own intent statement for RR says development there 'should rely predominantly on individual wells and septic tank systems.' No HOA culture — these are individually owned rural parcels, not covenanted subdivisions.
facts.who_lives_there: Working families, year-round. ZIP 28420: population 2,658, median age 46.3, median household income $53,935. Of 2,097 residents aged 16+, 1,196 are employed and 901 not in the labor force. Racially about 85% White, 6% Black (margins of error are wide — ±700 on total population — because this is a small rural ZCTA). This is the opposite of the beaches: people who live here all year, own their homes, drive to work, and are decades from retirement. The nearest thing to a tourist is a golfer driving NC 130 to Shallotte.

facts.strongest_angle: Lead with SHADE AND SALT UNDER A MARITIME FOREST CANOPY ON ACRE LOTS — the specific, physical reason lawns fail in Briarcliffe Acres and nowhere else in this batch. This is the wealthiest and oldest-skewing address in the entire service area (median age 60.7, median household income $156,250, median home value $760,600, 94.1% owner-occupied) on one-acre wooded lots where warm-season grass cannot hold under mature live oaks and where salt aerosol burns the oceanfront row. The second lead is the retiree backyard putting green: a 60-something owner with an acre of shaded ground, $156k income and no architectural committee to satisfy is the single best putting-green prospect inside the drawn polygon. The third lead — and the one that proves you have actually worked in this town — is naming the constraint out loud: the Public Tree Ordinance #2022.04 and the Bird Sanctuary / Certified Wildlife Habitat designations, and saying explicitly that you install without damaging protected root plates, using a permeable base that keeps the canopy alive. Also name the permitting reality correctly: the Town's building official issues the permit, the Association is not an HOA. Getting that distinction right is a credibility signal every Briarcliffe homeowner will recognise and no competitor's template page will contain. This page must read NOTHING like Atlantic Beach a mile up the same sand (opposite economics, opposite tenure) and nothing like a Burgess golf-subdivision page (there is no HOA here to submit to).
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: Actual ordinances on the town's books that bear on this work: Public Tree Ordinance #2022.04, which carries a required replacement-tree list; Ordinance #2025.04 governing golf cart operation (and no motor vehicles on the beaches); Ordinance #2025.02, beach regulations, Article II; Ordinance #2023.03 governing appeals to Town Council. Town is a designated Bird Sanctuary (1973) and Community Wildlife Habitat (2006); Habitat Park is a designated wildlife habitat. NO artificial-turf-specific rule was found — and there is no HOA architectural committee, because the Association is a nonprofit common-areas manager, not an HOA. The live constraint is therefore the TREE ORDINANCE plus wildlife-habitat status: excavating a compacted aggregate base inside the root plate of a protected mature live oak is the real permitting and liability risk in this town, and the town's own building official (Brandon Gray) signs the permit. GAP: full ordinance text was not retrievable — the town site (townofbriarcliffe.us) was only partially readable and Municode returned 403. Call Town Hall at 843.272.8863 to confirm tree-protection radii and any land-disturbance threshold before publishing specifics.
facts.turf_specifics: Two physical facts define this town and nothing else in the batch shares both. FIRST, SHADE: the community sits in mature maritime forest — live oak and yaupon canopy over acre lots — which is precisely why warm-season turf (St. Augustine, centipede) goes thin and patchy here; the town is a designated Bird Sanctuary (1973) and Certified Wildlife Habitat (2006) specifically because that canopy was preserved. SECOND, SALT: direct oceanfront aerosol on the front row along 3,500 ft of Atlantic frontage. Additionally, two spring-fed freshwater lakes — North Lake (~5.2 acres) and South Lake (~3.4 acres) — sit inside the town, meaning a high and seasonally variable water table across the interior. Substrate is coastal dune and maritime-forest sand: fast-draining, low organic matter, high root competition under the oaks. Storm exposure is documented and remembered — Hurricane Hazel destroyed the original community cabana in 1954.
facts.housing_stock: 0.64 sq mi, all land, elevation 30 ft, between Myrtle Beach and North Myrtle Beach with US 17 forming the northern border. Origin: Kenneth C. Ellsworth bought 600 acres in 1946 through his Yaupon Acres corporation — 3,500 ft of Atlantic oceanfront running roughly 6,000 ft inland to the Intracoastal Waterway — and platted it as a retirement community named for Briarcliff Manor, New York. Homes sit on ACRE-SIZED LOTS in mature maritime forest, not on a subdivision grid. Dominant era is 1950s-1970s custom coastal houses, with continuous renovation and teardown/rebuild since; 221 housing units at the 2000 census, ~186 households now. Median property value $760,600 (DataUSA 2024); active listings roughly $575,000 to $1.6M. Homeownership 94.1%, of which 71.9% carry a mortgage. Overwhelmingly year-round primary residences — this is NOT a rental market (contrast Atlantic Beach at 23.3% owner-occupied a mile up the beach). HOA STATUS IS THE SUBTLE AND IMPORTANT POINT: the Briarcliffe Acres Association is a nonprofit that owns and manages common areas (beachfront, parks, the two lakes) and explicitly states it is NOT an HOA. The Town of Briarcliffe Acres — incorporated Feb 25, 1976 after a 126-86 vote, with a mayor, four-member council, its own building official and its own police force — handles utilities, road maintenance, building permits and governance. So a turf job here is permitted by a two-employee town hall, not approved by an architectural review board.
facts.who_lives_there: Affluent retirees and semi-retired professionals. Median age 60.7 — the oldest in this batch. Median household income $156,250; median property value $760,600; poverty 9.38%; 88.8% insured. Population 448-479. Ranked among South Carolina's richest municipalities (MSN 4th richest, 2024; Forbes 6th richest, 2023); mean household income reported at $134,375 in 2022 data. Racially 96.24% White non-Hispanic. Top occupations: health diagnosing & treating practitioners (34) and business/financial (32) out of only 192 employed. Founded expressly as a retirement community; shifted somewhat family-ward after Hurricane Hazel insurance settlements and Myrtle Beach AFB expansion, but the age profile has swung back. Early residents included Dutch families and Col. Francis 'Gabby' Gabreski. No tourists — the beach is private.

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH: the backyard putting green on land you can actually afford, in the only place on this list where nobody has to ask permission. Longs is the golf-obsessed inland half-acre. Four courses sit inside the community — a Nicklaus (Long Bay), a 27-hole Tom Jackson (Aberdeen), Colonial Charters and Crown Park — so the customer is demonstrably a golfer; the lots are the biggest and cheapest in the batch; large stretches of the SC 9 / SC 905 corridor have NO HOA; and because Longs is unincorporated there is no town zoning counter while Horry County's stormwater ordinance exempts single-family residential. So make it a build-your-green page: multi-hole layouts, fringe and rough, real breaks — these people have the room. Second half handles the other Longs customer: the brand-new subdivision buyer standing on scraped, compacted fill that will not grow grass, watering a big lot off a well. WHY THIS DIFFERS FROM ITS NEIGHBOURS: Surfside Beach is 6,000 sq ft lots with a codified impervious cap and salt air — the opposite constraint set. Forestbrook is a flooding story. Little River / North Myrtle Beach are waterway and tourist. Longs is the only one whose honest lead is space, golf, no HOA, no permit. Keep flooding, salt spray and HOA-approval hand-holding OFF this page — none of it is the local truth.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: Longs is UNINCORPORATED — no town council, no municipal zoning counter, no town ordinance. Horry County governs. The Horry County Stormwater Management and Sediment Control Ordinance (effective Oct 1, 2000) requires a stormwater permit for land disturbance of 0.5 acre or more, BUT single-family residential construction, agricultural uses, timbering and minor residential subdivisions are EXEMPT — so the ordinary residential turf install in Longs is essentially unpermitted at county level. That 'no red tape' point is genuinely true for Longs in a way it is not for Surfside Beach. The binding constraint here is instead HOA covenants in the newer subdivisions (Sun Colony, Chestnut Farms, Colonial Charters, Tullamore Lakes), which are recorded documents a homeowner can pull. Horry County Stormwater: 843-381-8000. NOT VERIFIED THIS SESSION (web-search budget exhausted): whether SC Code Title 27 Ch. 30 (SC Homeowners Association Act) requires covenants be recorded with the Horry County Register of Deeds to be enforceable, and confirmation that SC has NO turf-preemption statute (unlike FL/TX/AZ). Confirm both before publishing.
facts.turf_specifics: Elevation 36 ft — the HIGHEST of the four places here, which matters: Longs drains better than Forestbrook or Surfside and carries none of their flood history. Coastal Plain sandy surface soils over tighter subsoil with a seasonal high water table is the regional norm (general Horry County characterisation, NOT a Longs-specific soil survey — verify against NRCS Web Soil Survey before publishing series names). No meaningful salt spray this far inland (~10–15 mi from the ocean). The real Longs turf problem is NEW-CONSTRUCTION SUBSOIL: production subdivisions scrape topsoil, compact the pad and hand over bare fill that will not hold sod, on large lots that are expensive to irrigate off a well. Different pain from Forestbrook's. Also: no municipal water/sewer on much of the rural corridor, so the septic drainfield is a genuine constraint on where a green or pet run can go.
facts.housing_stock: Checked 2026-09-07. Longs is NOT one housing stock — it is three, and a page that blurs them will read as generic. (1) Rural legacy: pre-1990 site-built and manufactured/modular homes on half-acre-to-multi-acre lots along SC 9, SC 905 and the county roads between them, largely NO HOA, well and septic common (H&H Builders markets manufactured/modular specifically to Longs, so the segment is real). (2) 1980s–90s golf-course subdivisions: Colonial Charters (course built 1988; homes, townhomes, patio homes and a large condo section), Long Bay, Aberdeen. (3) The current wave of production-builder HOA subdivisions: DRB Homes' Bluffs at Sun Colony and Chestnut Farms, Great Southern Homes' Longs communities, Beverly Homes' The Village at Longs, plus 55+ active-adult product. Very little seasonal rental. This is the 'I live here every day and I mow this myself' customer — the opposite of Surfside's absentee weekly-rental owner.

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH DRAINAGE, NOT LOOKS. Socastee is the only town on this list where the pitch writes itself around water. This is the community that flooded in Matthew (2016) and Florence (2018) — the Intracoastal crested at 21.8 ft — and where Horry County has since June 2022 closed on 31 flood-prone properties in Rosewood Estates, Bridge Creek and Lawson's Landing, funded by $13M+ in federal buyout money on top of $15.6M in 2021 flood-mitigation funding. Under the sod, the science says the same thing the homeowner already knows: Leon-type flatwoods sand with a hardpan at 15–22 inches and a water table 6–18 inches down means the yard is a mud pit from October to March and a mosquito farm afterward. So this page should be about what happens BENEATH the turf — excavation depth, geotextile, aggregate spec, positive-outlet drainage — while every neighbouring town's page talks about appearance. Secondary lead: Socastee is the youngest (median age 41), most year-round, most kid-dense of the four, so this is the page that should carry the pet-turf and sports-field offer — Socastee High, Forestbrook, HGTC on the doorstep and Grand Park and Ripken up 501 — not the beach-house putting-green offer. That is the opposite of Little River (retiree/snowbird), Garden City (rental turnover) and Red Hill (HOA approval).
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: (1) Horry County Stormwater Management and Sediment Control Ordinance, effective 1 Oct 2000: a stormwater permit is required for land-disturbing activity of one-half (0.5) acre or more; single-family residential construction is EXEMPT. So a residential back-yard turf install triggers no county stormwater permit, while a half-acre-plus commercial pad, daycare play yard or ball field does. (2) Unincorporated — there is no municipal architectural review; the binding constraint is the subdivision's covenants. Under the SC Homeowners Association Act (SC Code Title 27, Ch. 30, effective 17 May 2018), an HOA's governing documents must be recorded with the Horry County Register of Deeds to be enforceable, and rules/regulations must be re-recorded annually by 10 January following adoption or amendment. That is a usable, checkable line for a Socastee page: a homeowner can look up whether the turf rule they were quoted is actually recorded. (3) HONEST NEGATIVE FINDING: no South Carolina statute was found granting homeowners a right to install artificial turf over HOA objection (SC is not among the states with turf-protection laws). (4) Flood: parcels in the Special Flood Hazard Area along the IWW fall under Horry County floodplain requirements — this could NOT be read directly (the county web server refused connections all session) and must be confirmed against the ordinance text before publishing.
facts.turf_specifics: This is the flood town, and everything technical should hang off that. Elevation ~20 ft; the Atlantic Intracoastal Waterway bisects the CDP. The IWW crested at 21.8 ft during Hurricane Florence (Sept 2018) and 19.2 ft during Hurricane Matthew (Oct 2016). Soils are Atlantic Coast Flatwoods sands — Leon-series and similar: USDA classes them very poorly to poorly drained, with a spodic (Bh) hardpan within 30 inches (typically 15–22 in) and a seasonal high water table commonly 6–18 in below surface, 0–6 in in depressions with standing water 6+ months a year. Permeability is moderate-to-moderately-rapid in the A/E horizons but moderate-to-moderately-SLOW through the Bh hardpan — meaning water moves down fast, hits the pan, and sits. Practical consequence: a turf base designed to infiltrate will pond. Base has to be excavated through or drained above the pan to a positive outlet, not dry-welled into saturated subgrade. Salt exposure is low — roughly 8–10 miles inland from open ocean, brackish influence only immediately along the waterway. Irrigation is not a limiting factor here; standing water is.
facts.housing_stock: Median year structure built 1994 — a 1980s–2000s subdivision belt laid over legacy rural parcels. ~10,077 housing units: 58.1% detached single-family, 14.4% mobile/manufactured (the highest manufactured-home share of the four towns in this batch), 2.6% attached/townhome. Median house/condo value ~$264,808 (2024); median household income $62,257; poverty 12.57%. 13.88 sq mi (13.37 land), elevation ~20 ft. Population 22,213 (2020 census, +11.3% over 2010), est. ~25,708 in 2026. 98.0% urban. Lot sizes: roughly 1/4–1/3 acre in the platted subdivisions (Palmetto Bays, The Bays, Forestbrook, Rosewood Estates, Bridge Creek, Lawson's Landing); noticeably larger half-acre-to-multi-acre legacy parcels along Dick Pond Road (SC 544), Hwy 707 and Enterprise Road. HOA coverage is PATCHY, not blanket — newer subdivisions have covenants, the older waterway and rural lots do not. Year-round owner-occupied, essentially zero second-home share.
facts.who_lives_there: Year-round working families — the most family-heavy and youngest of the four. Median age 41.0; 20.7% under 18; 19.7% aged 65+. Racially 73.3% white, 13.8% Hispanic or Latino (the largest Hispanic share in this batch), 7.5% Black. These are Myrtle Beach service-industry, hospital, school-district and trades households living inland of the beach, not tourists and not snowbirds.
