facts.strongest_angle: Do NOT write a lawn page. Atlantic Beach's economy is short-term rental and festival tourism on four blocks of oceanfront sand, with 23.3% homeownership, $33,500 median household income and 29.5% poverty — the lowest-income beachfront in the polygon. LEAD with the vacation-rental owner's revenue problem: a rental cottage two blocks off the ocean cannot hold a green lawn — pure sand, constant salt spray, and nobody on site to water between guests — and a bare, scorched sand yard costs bookings and review scores. That is a return-on-investment argument, and it is the only argument that works at this income level. SECOND lead: the town's own event ground and rights-of-way for Bikefest (Memorial Day) and the Gullah Geechee Festival (August) — thousands of people standing on sand and worn grass for a weekend, twice a year, then nine months to recover. THIRD, and this is a condition rather than a selling point: handle the town's identity with genuine accuracy and respect — the Black Pearl, chartered 1966, one of the very few Black-owned and governed oceanfront towns in America, Gullah Geechee heritage, the marker at 717 Atlantic Street. Cite the marker, get the dates right, and do not use the history as decoration or the page will do more harm than good. This page must read nothing like Briarcliffe Acres one mile up the same beach — identical sand, identical salt, completely opposite economics and tenure. If the client wants volume, this town is a low-yield page that earns its place on authenticity and local-knowledge signal, not on lead count; say that to him plainly.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: NONE FOUND — and this is a genuine research failure, not an absence. The Town of Atlantic Beach website returned HTTP 403 and library.municode.com returned 403, so the town's zoning and building code could not be read at all; horrycountysc.gov refused connections throughout. There is no HOA. Constraints that certainly apply and MUST be checked before any ordinance claim goes on the page: SCDHEC-OCRM beachfront jurisdictional and setback lines govern any work seaward of the setback on this stretch, and state coastal construction rules apply. Call Town Hall at 717 Atlantic Street before publishing anything ordinance-specific. Do not assert a turf rule, a fence rule or an impervious-surface rule for this town on current evidence.
facts.turf_specifics: The harshest salt exposure in the batch — four blocks of direct oceanfront with constant salt aerosol. Substrate is beach and dune sand: extremely fast-draining, essentially no organic matter, no water-holding capacity, which is exactly why natural turf here demands constant irrigation and fertiliser and still washes out and burns. Shallow water table, storm-surge exposure, and a founding trauma that residents still reference — Hurricane Hazel in 1954. The flip side is the sales argument: because the native sand IS a drainage layer, a properly ballasted synthetic system installs fast and drains without an engineered sub-drain, which is not true in Burgess. GAP: no soil-series source obtained (NRCS timeout); the dune-sand characterisation is inferred from oceanfront geography, not from a soil survey.
facts.housing_stock: 0.16 sq mi — four blocks of oceanfront, bounded by the Windy Hill and Crescent Beach sections of North Myrtle Beach. Elevation 30 ft. The Atlantic Beach Company subdivided the tract into 100+ residential and commercial lots in the 1940s; Hurricane Hazel (1954) destroyed most oceanfront structures and owners were underinsured, so much of it was never rebuilt. Result: small mid-century frame cottages, scattered later infill, new short-term-rental construction, and a large share of vacant or undeveloped platted lots. 244 housing units at the 2000 census; DataUSA now shows only 116. Median property value $385,000 — that is oceanfront LAND value, not house value, and it sits beside a $33,500 median household income, which is the tell. HOMEOWNERSHIP IS ONLY 23.3%, by far the lowest in this batch (Briarcliffe Acres is 94.1%) — most occupied units are rentals. Lots are small beach-town lots, not acre lots. No HOA — this is a chartered municipality (1966), one of the few Black-owned and governed oceanfront communities in the United States. POPULATION FIGURES CONFLICT AND SHOULD BE HANDLED HONESTLY: 195 (2020 census per Wikipedia), 483 (2020 per SC Encyclopedia), 237 (DataUSA ACS), 472 (2025 estimate). At this size ACS estimates are unreliable; do not present one number as settled.
facts.who_lives_there: Predominantly Black or African American — 45.13% Black non-Hispanic, 39.49% White non-Hispanic, 6.15% Hispanic/Latino (2020); DataUSA shows 143 Black residents of 237. Most property is still owned by African Americans. Median age 41.5 — markedly younger than Briarcliffe Acres (60.7) or Loris (51.2). Median household income $33,500, down 16.3% year over year; 29.5% below the poverty line; only 118 employed, down 22.4%. With 23.3% homeownership, the resident base is largely year-round renters, alongside a growing vacation-rental inventory. Massive seasonal visitor swing relative to resident count: Atlantic Beach Bikefest over Memorial Day weekend (descended from the Carolina Knight Riders rally begun in 1980) and the Gullah Geechee Festival in late August (established 2001) draw crowds many multiples of the population. Culturally rooted in Gullah Geechee heritage and part of the Gullah Geechee Cultural Heritage Corridor.
facts.golf: No course in town — the town is four blocks. The adjacency is the North Myrtle Beach courses along US 17. VERIFY BEFORE NAMING ANY: beachwoodgolfclub.com did not resolve and azaleasands.com is now a parked domain-sale page, which may indicate closure — several North Myrtle Beach courses have shut for redevelopment. Do not name a nearby course on this page without confirming it is still open. Golf is a weak angle here regardless; this is not the town's economy.
facts.commercial_targets: THIN, AND THE PAGE SHOULD SAY SO RATHER THAN PAD. There are no schools inside town (Horry County Schools serves it), no sports complex, no verified daycares and no verified pet businesses. The realistic named targets are: the Town of Atlantic Beach itself — town-owned parcels and the pavilion/event ground used for Bikefest and the Gullah Geechee Festival — and the growing set of vacation-rental owners and operators driving the town's current revitalization. GAP: business-level verification was impossible (search budget exhausted; town site 403; directories blocked). Run a Maps pass on 29582/Atlantic Beach before writing a commercial section, but set expectations: with 116 housing units and 118 employed residents, there is very little commercial base here.
facts.landmarks: Town Hall at 717 Atlantic Street — the SC historical marker reading 'Atlantic Beach / The Black Pearl,' erected by the Atlantic Beach Historical Society in 2005, stands here (GPS 33 deg 48.323' N, 78 deg 43.101' W). The town is wedged between the Windy Hill and Crescent Beach sections of North Myrtle Beach. Cultural murals through the town. Atlantic Beach Bikefest, Memorial Day weekend. Gullah Geechee Festival, late August. The Gullah Geechee Cultural Heritage Corridor. The 'Black Pearl of the Grand Strand' nickname. Chartered 1966 under first mayors Emery Gore and Millard Rucker; developed from 1934 by George W. Tyson, who bought 47 acres, then by the Atlantic Beach Company (J.W. Seabrook, R.K. Gordon, P.C. Kelly III) from 1943.

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH WATER. Forestbrook is the flood page. This is the one town in the batch where the customer has personally watched their yard hold water — Socastee Swamp is literally the southeastern boundary, elevation is 23 ft, the basin drains to a Socastee Creek that admittedly cannot cope, and Horry County is spending millions on culverts and flood-benching plus an $846,450 mitigation grant right here. So the page must NOT open with 'never mow again.' It opens with the base: what goes under the turf, how deep, why the aggregate has no fines in it, where the water goes, and an honest line about rain-on-turf versus a water table rising through it. That honesty is the conversion mechanism — it is the one thing a Forestbrook homeowner has been lied to about by every other quote. Back it with the second Forestbrook truth: 91.5% owner-occupied, 89.8% same house a year ago — nobody here is flipping, so a 15–20 year warranty argument lands and would be wasted on a Surfside rental owner. WHY THIS DIFFERS FROM ITS NEIGHBOURS: Surfside's constraint is a written impervious cap and salt air on a 6,000 sq ft lot. Longs' is compacted new-build subsoil on a big dry lot at 36 ft. Carolina Forest next door is the master-planned HOA-approval story. Forestbrook's constraint is standing water — and no other page in this batch should be allowed to use that lead.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: Unincorporated — Horry County governs, no municipal code. Horry County Stormwater Management and Sediment Control Ordinance (eff. Oct 1, 2000): stormwater permit required at 0.5 acre or more of land disturbance, with single-family residential construction, agricultural uses, timbering and minor residential subdivisions EXEMPT. In Forestbrook say the opposite of what most turf sites say: the ABSENCE of a permit requirement is exactly why the drainage design has to be right, because nobody is checking it for you. Horry County Stormwater: 843-381-8000. Live, checkable local project: the Forestbrook Road widening to a 5-lane corridor with sidewalks and bike facilities (USACE permit action SAC-2023-01053) — road work changes runoff patterns on adjoining lots. HOA: subdivision-by-subdivision, no blanket rule. NOT VERIFIED: whether Horry County counts artificial turf as impervious for any calculation — county sources do not address it, and Raleigh NC's '100% impervious unless engineered' treatment is NOT a Horry County rule; do not import it.
facts.turf_specifics: This field carries the whole page. Forestbrook's southeastern border IS SOCASTEE SWAMP (per the CDP's own geographic definition). Elevation 23 ft — the lowest figure in this batch. US 501 bounds it northeast, SC 31 (Carolina Bays Parkway) northwest, so it sits in the bottom of a bowl: water comes down out of Carolina Forest and bottlenecks at Socastee Creek, the primary drainage for both Socastee and Forestbrook, which cannot handle volume in a Florence-scale event or even after several straight rainy days. Horry County has committed $2M+ to Socastee/Forestbrook flood projects including a second large culvert under McCormick Road and flood-benching, plus an $846,450 CDBG-MIT grant specifically for Forestbrook-area flood mitigation; residents have publicly criticised the county's response. Practical consequence: the base build IS the product here — open-graded aggregate with fines washed out, generous depth, perforated drain lines tied to positive daylight or an existing swale, high-flow perforated backing, and honest talk about the difference between rain falling on turf and a water table rising through it. Regional soils are sandy over tighter, poorly drained subsoil with a high seasonal water table (general Horry County characterisation — verify against NRCS Web Soil Survey before naming series). No salt exposure: ~5 mi inland.
facts.housing_stock: Checked 2026-09-07. Suburban single-family dominant, with some townhomes and condos. Two layers: older non-HOA homes and small acreage tracts along Forestbrook Road itself (many pre-1990, deep lots, mature pine and hardwood), and 1990s–2020s HOA subdivisions filling in behind them — Forestbrook Estates among the named ones. The CDP grew 44.3% between the 2010 census (4,612) and 2020 (6,656); Census QuickFacts puts the July 1 2025 estimate at 7,273 — so a large share of the stock is genuinely new. Estimated median house/condo value $363,378 (2023); current median listing ~$364,900 at ~67 days on market. Owner-occupancy 91.5% — the highest in this batch by a wide margin. Lot sizes vary hard: quarter-acre in newer subdivisions, half-acre-plus on older Forestbrook Road frontage. HOA prevalence is MIXED and the mix matters — newer subdivisions have boards, the older road frontage does not.
facts.who_lives_there: The most rooted, least transient population in this batch. 89.8% lived in the same house one year ago. 91.5% own. 27.5% are 65+, 16.5% under 18 — retirees AND working families with school-age kids, not a resort population. Average commute ~24.7 minutes. 2020 composition: 80.92% white non-Hispanic, 6.19% Hispanic, 6.01% Black, 1.08% Asian, 5.36% other/mixed. Zero tourist economy, essentially no vacation-rental stock. These people will still be in the house in ten years — the right audience for a 15–20 year product argument rather than a resale-value one.
facts.golf: No course inside the CDP, but it is wrapped by them. Immediately adjacent: ARROWHEAD COUNTRY CLUB, 1201 Burcale Road, Myrtle Beach SC 29579 — 27 holes (Lakes, Cypress and Waterway nines), Tom Jackson and Raymond Floyd, opened 1995, Bermuda fairways and bent-grass greens along the Intracoastal Waterway. Burcale Road is the direct connector off Forestbrook Road, so Arrowhead is the course a Forestbrook local actually names. The US 501 corridor forming Forestbrook's northeast boundary carries the Myrtle Beach National group and the Legends/Wizard/Man O' War cluster within minutes — VERIFY exact names, addresses and current operation before publishing; I could not confirm those individually this session.
facts.commercial_targets: FORESTBROOK ELEMENTARY SCHOOL, 4000 Panthers Pkwy — 881 students, 15:1 ratio, National Blue Ribbon School (2012; one source claims three-time — verify the count before printing). FORESTBROOK MIDDLE SCHOOL, 4430 Gator Lane — 820 students, grades 6–8, Socastee attendance area. SOCASTEE HIGH SCHOOL (attendance-area high school, IB Diploma Programme). ARROWHEAD COUNTRY CLUB (27 holes — practice green, tee line, clubhouse). The Forestbrook/Socastee retail corridor along US 501 and SC 707. Horry County Schools is a 58-school district across nine attendance areas — a district-level playground-surfacing and field conversation is the real prize, and Forestbrook is a credible foot in the door because both schools sit inside the CDP. NOT VERIFIED: named daycares and pet daycares in 29579 — pull from Google Maps and SC DSS childcare licensing before the page ships.
facts.landmarks: Forestbrook Road itself (the spine, being widened to five lanes). Socastee Swamp / Socastee Creek. McCormick Road (site of the planned culvert). Carolina Bays Parkway / SC 31 along the northwest edge; US 501 along the northeast. Forestbrook Elementary at 4000 Panthers Pkwy. Forestbrook Middle at 4430 Gator Lane. Arrowhead Country Club on Burcale Road. Coastal Carolina University and Tanger Outlets are the usual 'close to' anchors. Forestbrook is 5 mi northwest of Myrtle Beach and 10 mi southeast of Conway.

facts.strongest_angle: LEAD WITH HOA-APPROVAL-READY INSTALLS, THEN THE COLLEGE NEXT DOOR. Red Hill has no waterfront, no pier, no historic district and no tourists — it is a 501/544 commuter belt of mid-1990s subdivisions sitting at 36 feet, the highest and best-drained ground in this batch. So the residential lead is the mirror image of Socastee's: not 'we'll fix your swamp' but 'your soil already drains — what fails here is Bermuda under a 95-degree August sun on a treeless lot, and an architectural review committee that wants a spec sheet before it says yes.' Build the page around the ARC submittal: pile height and colour matched to the covenant, edge and transition detail that reads as lawn from the street, a submittable product data sheet, and the SC HOA Act fact that an unrecorded restriction is unenforceable. Then the commercial half carries the heaviest institutional-turf list in the entire service area, because Coastal Carolina University's athletic campus is at the CDP's edge: Brooks Stadium's distinctive teal Shaw turf went in in 2015 and is at replacement age, Springs Brooks is still grass, and Carolina Forest High plus the Ripken Experience are minutes down 501. Red Hill is the page a sports-field landing page should point at — while Socastee gets the drainage story and Little River gets the municipal ball fields.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: (1) Same Horry County Stormwater Management and Sediment Control Ordinance as Socastee: 0.5-acre land-disturbance trigger for a stormwater permit; single-family residential construction exempt. (2) HOA is the real gate here. Unincorporated means no municipal architectural review, but the Carolina Forest-era master-planned covenants with active architectural review committees are the norm across Red Hill's housing stock — turf approval is an ARC submittal question, not a county question. (3) SC Homeowners Association Act (Title 27, Ch. 30, effective 17 May 2018): governing documents must be recorded with the Horry County Register of Deeds to be enforceable, and rules must be re-recorded annually by 10 January. Unrecorded restrictions lose enforceability — genuinely useful to a Red Hill homeowner whose ARC has said no. (4) HONEST NEGATIVE FINDING: no SC statute found overriding an HOA's ability to prohibit artificial turf.
facts.turf_specifics: The high, dry one. At 36 ft elevation on a sand ridge, Red Hill has the best natural drainage of the four — upland Coastal Plain sands rather than the depressional flatwoods that define Socastee. But it is a two-soil town: ridge lots drain, while the CDP's western edge drops into the Waccamaw River floodplain and the Waccamaw National Wildlife Refuge, and Waccamaw River Park is documented as susceptible to occasional flooding. Salt exposure: effectively nil at 12–13 miles inland — no salt-spray corrosion concern on fasteners or infill, which distinguishes the spec from Little River and Garden City. What actually kills lawns here is heat load and UV on open, unshaded 501-corridor lots, plus compaction on new-construction subgrade that was scraped and re-graded during the 1990s–2000s build-out. Spec the conversation around infill temperature, UV-stable fibre and shade-free full-sun performance, not around water.
facts.housing_stock: Median year structure built 1995 — a 1990s–2000s commuter-belt suburb, functionally the eastern half of the Carolina Forest development wave. 7,034 housing units; 6,244 occupied, of which 74.17% owner-occupied and 25.83% renter. Estimated median house/condo value $272,290 (2023); older or smaller homes trade $200K–$350K, larger modern homes $400K–$650K. Average household income $73,042, median $62,132. 11.09 sq mi. ELEVATION 36 FT — the highest of the four by a wide margin; the 'hill' is a real relict sand ridge standing above the Waccamaw floodplain. Population 10,509 (2000) → 13,223 (2010) → 15,906 (2020); ~15,920 in the 2020–2024 ACS. 94.4% urban. Described as 'sparse suburban.' Named subdivision: Red Hill Commons. HOA-HEAVY — this is the most covenant-governed of the four, because the housing is dominated by platted 1990s–2000s subdivisions with architectural review committees along US 501 and SC 544; the legacy parcels toward SC 90 and the Waccamaw are the exception. Year-round, not seasonal.
facts.who_lives_there: A mix of young professionals and retirees; residents skew conservative and overwhelmingly own rather than rent. Median age 45.4. Racial composition 71.09% white (non-Hispanic), 11.02% Black, 11.0% Hispanic or Latino, 1.57% Asian. The population is here for schools and commute — Coastal Carolina University, Conway Medical Center and Conway to the north, Myrtle Beach and the airport 12–13 miles south. There is no tourist economy and effectively no second-home stock.
facts.golf: The Wizard and The Man O'War (Dan Maples, Carolina Forest) and The Witch — Carolina Forest is built around this Maples trio. Wild Wing Golf Course, 1000 Wild Wing Blvd, Conway (27 holes, ~5.6 miles). Legends Golf & Resort, 1500 Legends Drive — Heathland and Parkland courses. King's North at Myrtle Beach National. The Hackler Course at Coastal Carolina University, 107 Citadel Drive, Conway. Arrowhead Country Club to the south.
facts.commercial_targets: THIS IS THE INSTITUTIONAL-FIELD TOWN. Coastal Carolina University athletics, One Landon Loop, Conway — physically on the Red Hill CDP's edge: Brooks Stadium (21,000 seats; Shaw Sports PowerBlade teal synthetic turf installed 2015, replacing natural grass — a decade-old field now at the end of a typical synthetic service life); Springs Brooks Stadium (baseball, 5,300 capacity, $15.2M 2015 renovation, STILL NATURAL GRASS — a live conversion target); CCU Soccer / St. John Stadium, 132 Chanticleer Drive West; CCU Indoor Practice Facility; HTC Center; Kimbel Arena; CCU beach volleyball and tennis courts; the on-campus TD Sports Complex. Schools: Carolina Forest High School; Carolina Forest Elementary; Waccamaw Elementary; Black Water Middle; Ten Oaks Middle; PALM Charter High School; Waccamaw Academy; A Touch of Christ Christian School; Conway Middle; Conway Elementary, 1101 Snowhill Drive; Conway Education Center; E. Craig Wall Jr. Memorial Stadium (Conway High football). Also on the 501 corridor: The Ripken Experience Myrtle Beach, Ripken Way Blvd, ZIP 29579 (a multi-field tournament baseball complex, in Myrtle Beach city limits but on Red Hill's doorstep). Parks/rec: Conway Recreation Complex; Conway Dog Park; Ten Oaks Park; Forestbrook Park. Pet: Carolina Forest Veterinary Hospital; Palmetto Animal Hospital; PetSmart; Pet Supplies Plus, 2300 Church Street, Conway; Petco, 2918 Church Street, Conway. DAYCARE IS A GAP — open-data searches surfaced almost no named licensed childcare centres inside the Red Hill CDP; this needs a windshield survey of the 501/544 corridor or a pull from the SC DSS licensed-facility register before that section is written.
facts.landmarks: Waccamaw River Park and its 1.2-mile Green Trail boardwalk (about a mile from Red Hill; roughly a 20-minute walk). Cox Ferry Lake Recreation Area within the Waccamaw National Wildlife Refuge. Wheels of Yesteryear vintage car museum. Nannie Annie's Breakfast & Lunch. US 501 and SC 544 (Corporal Dennis Lyden Memorial Highway) are the two spines everyone navigates by. Coastal Carolina University's athletics campus at One Landon Loop sits right at the CDP's northern edge. Conway Medical Center. Tanger Outlets on 501.

facts.strongest_angle: Loris is the one town in this batch where the money is NOT in the yard, and the page has to admit that in its structure. Median household income is $36,899 with 23% poverty — a five-figure backyard putting green is not the lead. What Loris has that no coastal town in the polygon has is (a) land with no covenants and (b) public ball fields a tiny city must maintain on a tiny budget. So lead with two things: FIRST, Heniford Field Park and Loris High School athletics — municipal and school field conversion framed as playable-days and maintenance-dollars, which is also exactly the commercial work the owner says he wants; SECOND, the acreage-without-an-HOA story — half-acre to five-acre rural lots where an owner can put in a real 3-5 hole practice green, a fenced pet run, or a batting-cage surface without asking an architectural committee, which is impossible in Burgess or Briarcliffe Acres. Add a third, quieter lead that is pure conversion: service radius. Loris is the northwest corner of the drawn service area, 30-plus minutes inland, and locals correctly assume beach contractors will not drive out. Stating plainly 'we come to Loris' is itself the differentiator. Voice: this is tobacco-and-railroad country — the Gate City, the Bog-Off, McLeod Loris, chicken bog. Use that vocabulary because it is checkable and it is how the audience describes itself. Explicitly do NOT reuse the coastal salt-and-shade copy from Briarcliffe Acres or the golf-community HOA copy from Burgess; neither applies 25 miles inland.
facts.ordinance_or_hoa: No artificial-turf-specific rule found at city or county level. IMPORTANT RESEARCH FAILURE: horrycountysc.gov refused connections on every attempt (ECONNREFUSED to 64.138.212.22) and library.municode.com returned 403, so neither the Horry County stormwater/land-disturbance ordinance nor the City of Loris code could be read; cityofloris.com also refused connection. The practically relevant point that IS supportable: rural parcels outside city limits are largely covenant-free (real estate listings sell 'no HOA restrictions' as a benefit), so the binding constraint on a Loris job is Horry County land-disturbance/stormwater permitting, not an architectural review committee. Verify county thresholds by phone before making a permitting claim on the page.
facts.turf_specifics: Inland northern Horry County on the Atlantic coastal plain — NO salt exposure, which is the single biggest physical difference from the other three places in this batch. Historically bright-leaf tobacco ground (Horry was South Carolina's top tobacco county by the 1920s, with Loris the largest tobacco market in the section by 1909), which implies well-drained sandy and sandy-loam coastal-plain ridge soils — tobacco will not grow on wet ground. Terrain is flat; Horry County's highest point countywide is 124 ft. The Waccamaw River and its swamp system lie west/southwest and the county is historically 'isolated by the many rivers and swamps typical of the South Carolina Lowcountry,' so low-lying parcels near the swamp margins will behave very differently from the ridge lots. Rural acreage is largely on private wells, so the irrigation-cost argument is weaker than on the coast where households pay GSWSA metered water. GAP: no soil-series-level source obtained — NRCS Horry County soil survey timed out; verify with USDA Web Soil Survey before making a series-specific claim.
facts.housing_stock: Small incorporated city, 4.57 sq mi, founded 1887 as a railroad town, incorporated 1902. Population 2,449 (2020 census) / 2,645 (DataUSA ACS). Median property value $214,300 (DataUSA); median sale price ~$269,385 over trailing 12 months, up 6% (Homes.com). Homeownership 55.7%. Stock is three layers: (1) pre-WWII and mid-century frame houses in the old railroad/tobacco core along Main Street and Railroad Avenue; (2) post-war ranches; (3) the dominant volume today — rural acreage parcels, site-built and manufactured/modular homes on roughly 0.5 to 5+ acre lots in the 29569 ZIP outside city limits. Roughly 160 land parcels listed for sale; houses-with-land average $142,273 per acre. HOA prevalence is LOW — listings actively advertise 'no HOA restrictions' as a feature. Year-round primary residences, not second homes, not seasonal rental. GAP: I could not retrieve a year-built distribution — city-data.com returned HTTP 429 and bestplaces redirected. Verify before publishing an era claim more specific than the above.
facts.who_lives_there: Year-round working families and retirees — no tourist or second-home component. Median household income $36,899; 23% of residents below the poverty line (vs 12.5% national). Median age 51.2 (DataUSA) / 47.4 (2020 census), with 25.1% aged 65 or older. Racial composition 54.1% White, 38.1% Black or African American, 4.6% Hispanic/Latino. Employment base is only 975 people: health care & social assistance (169), accommodation & food services (154), retail trade (150). Average commute 31.6 minutes, 82.6% driving alone — a large share of the working population commutes southeast to Myrtle Beach / North Myrtle Beach service jobs and comes home to cheap land. This is the lowest-income town in the batch alongside Atlantic Beach.
facts.golf: No course inside the city. Per the Loris Chamber of Commerce, within a 10-mile radius: Crown Park Golf Club (18), Woodland Valley Country Club (18), and Aberdeen Country Club (27 holes). Golf is a weak lead here — Loris is roughly 25-30 miles inland from the Grand Strand golf corridor.
facts.commercial_targets: HIGHEST-VALUE MUNICIPAL TARGET IN THIS TOWN: Heniford Field Park — children's playground, picnic shelters, tennis courts and 'several baseball and soccer fields' (Loris Chamber). A city of 2,500 with a $36,899 median household income maintaining multiple grass diamonds and soccer pitches is a maintenance-budget conversation, not an aesthetics one. Schools (Horry County Schools): Loris High School (Lions), Loris Middle School, Loris Elementary School, Daisy Elementary; Green Sea Floyds schools just north. Also: McLeod Health Loris hospital campus; Playcard Environmental Education Center; Loris Senior Citizens Center (in Loris Garden Apartments); downtown's 20+ restaurants and specialty shops. GAP: named daycares and pet businesses could NOT be verified — the WebSearch budget was exhausted and business directories (city-data, golflink, municode, chamber directory) all returned 403/404/429. Run a Google Business/Maps pass on 29569 for daycare, veterinary, kennel and grooming before writing that section.
facts.landmarks: Downtown Main Street and Railroad Avenue (2002 revitalization added sidewalks, street lamps and a city clock); Bank of Loris building, 1907, the first brick building constructed in Loris; the 1911 railroad depot; the 'Gate City' nickname earned in 1914 as the first town on the railroad south of the North Carolina line; the Great Loris Bog-Off Festival (third Saturday in October, celebrating chicken bog — chicken, rice, sausage and spices); Small Town, Big Show Festival (third Saturday in April); Heniford Field Park; Playcard Environmental Education Center (~4 miles from downtown); Loris branch of the Horry County library (14,000+ volumes); Twin City Airport; WLSC-AM radio (on air since 1958); McLeod Health Loris, opened as Loris Community Hospital on May 15, 1950; Loris Wood Products furniture factory (1946). Robert H. Brooks, founder of Hooters, was from Loris.
